The Alveo Vera is a cold-loving plant that consumes Carbon Dioxide and Ice to produce Oxylite, which offgasses into breathable Oxygen after harvesting. Alveo Veras can be found growing naturally within the Ice Cave Biome.


== Seed ==
Alveo Vera Seed can be obtained by harvesting and uprooting Alveo Vera, or by digging up a Buried Object within the Ice Cave Biome. It grows into Alveo Vera when planted.


== Usage ==
Due to their availability and the abundance of Ice in the starting Ice Cave Biome, Alveo Vera plants are often the first source of sustainable Oxygen that a player will make use of when starting on the Ceres Asteroid or its Spaced Out variants.


=== Domestic & Wild Growth ===


==== Domestic ====
Domestic Alveo Veras inhale 1200g/cycle (2g/s) of Carbon Dioxide and consume 20kg/cycle (~33.33g/s) of Ice as fertilizer. They take 2 cycles to grow, dropping 36kg of Oxylite when harvested, resulting in a maximum theoretical output of up to 18kg/cycle (30g/s) of Oxylite per domestic plant (assuming no buffs).


==== Wild ====
Wild Alveo Veras inhale 300g/cycle (0.5g/s) of Carbon Dioxide. They take 8 cycles to grow, dropping 36kg of Oxylite when harvested, resulting in a maximum output of 4.5kg/cycle (7.5g/s) of Oxylite per wild plant (assuming no buffs).


=== Oxygen & Carbon Dioxide Economy ===
Below are two tables comparing the production and consumption of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide between Duplicants and Alveo Veras (without growth buffs).

Note that since mature Alveo Veras temporarily stop producing Oxylite until they are harvested, the maximum amount of Oxygen that they can produce will always be less than the theoretical maximum during gameplay.

As shown in the graph above, at least ~3.33 domestic (or ~13.33 wild) Alveo Veras are required to create enough Oxygen to sustain one Duplicant. However, each domestic Alveo Vera consumes the same amount of Carbon Dioxide exhaled by one Duplicant (2 g/s). Therefore, assuming all of the Carbon Dioxide being exhaled by Duplicants is being fed back to Alveo Veras, the remaining plants will need to have additional Carbon Dioxide supplied. This means that regardless of whether domestic or wild plants are used, at least 4.67 g/s of additional Carbon Dioxide will have to be created per Duplicant.

The ratio of Oxygen Produced to Carbon Dioxide Consumed can be substantially increased by applying growth speed buffs via Farmer's Touch, pollination, and/or mutations.


=== Water to Oxygen Economy ===
Because one domestic Alveo Vera converts 33.33g/s of Ice into 30g/s of Oxylite, the regular domestic Alveo Vera's maximum theoretical conversion rate of Water to Oxygen is 90%.

The conversion rate can be substantially increased (even above 100%) by applying growth speed buffs via Farmer's Touch/Grubgrub Rub/plant mutations.


=== Mutation Requirements ===
Specialized requires temperatures -60 °C ↔ -20 °C / -76 °F ↔ -4 °F. Superspecialized requires temperatures -48 °C ↔ -32 °C / -54.4 °F ↔ -25.6 °F.


== Database ==
Alveo Vera
Plant

The Alveo Vera's fleshy stems are dotted with small apertures featuring bidirectional valves through which Carbon Dioxide is absorbed and sticky oxygenated waste is secreted.The buildup from this respiration cycle crystallizes into Oxylite ore.Horticulturists have long been curious about the protective epithelium that prevents the Oxylite ore from sublimating while on the plant. Unfortunately, it is too fragile to survive handling, and has thus far proven impossible to study.

Arbor Tree grows branches that can be harvested for Wood. It is found naturally in Forest Biome.


== Seed ==
The Arbor Acorn is the seed of Arbor Tree.  It requires one unit of empty space on the left and right to allow room for the branches to grow. It can initially be obtained by uprooting an arbor tree, digging buried objects in forest biomes, and random printing pod care packages.
As the tree itself does not have harvestable items, it can not directly produce new Arbor Acorns like traditional plants. Instead, spawning or harvesting branches has a 5% chance of producing an Arbor Acorn inside the trunk. A Pip or Cuddle Pip is then needed to "rummage" the tree, which drops an acorn on the Arbor Tree. There is no in-game way to detect if an Arbor Acorn is stored inside the trunk.


== Usage ==
Pips consume the growing Arbor Tree branches and excrete Dirt.


== Growth ==
Arbor Tree requires a temperature range of 15 °C ↔ 40 °C / 59 °F ↔ 104 °F, and an air pressure of 0.15 kg ↔ 10 kg. 
Arbor Trees grow in two stages: In the first stage, taking a complete growth cycle (18 or 4.5 Cycles), it grows the main trunk and produces no wood. The second stage takes another growth cycle and produces branches. Arbor Trees can have up to 5 branches in 7 possible locations (the center-center and center-bottom are occupied by the trunk). Once a branch has matured, it can be harvested by a dupe or will self-harvest after 20 cycles. Each branch produces 300 kg Wood. 
An Arbor Tree requires 3x3 space for all 5 branches to grow, centered on the tile two spaces above the tile the trunk is planted, so growth can be stifled by nearby walls and buildings.
Arbor Trees consume 70 kg of Polluted Water and 10 kg of Dirt regardless of the number of branches growing; therefore, it is best to grow Arbor Trees with 5 branches (in a 3x3 space) to reduce the amount of resources spent.
The 5 branches can grow from any of 7 different locations (3 on each side, 1 on top).  You can select individual branches to see their growth progress.  Individual branches may also be "uprooted" individually and separately from the main trunk, forcing the branch to regrow in another of the 7 spawn locations (if any are available).  If a branch is blocked from growing by an obstacle, removing that obstacle (including a branch from an adjacent tree that is occupying that spot) will immediately permit a branch to spawn in that location (if the tree is not already at 5).  Once a branch has spawned in a location, it will continue to regrow in that same location unless and until forced to move by a manual uproot command.
Using manual uprooting (a one-time process when they first start to grow their branches), it is possible to grow up to 3 Arbor Trees with only a single empty tile between them (rather than the normal 2).  The two outer trees use the top slot all 3 outside slots, plus 1 of the slots in the shared tile with the inner tree, while the inner tree uses its own top slot and 2 of the 3 slots in each of the shared tiles.  Planting 4 or more with this spacing does not permit all branches to spawn.  One can plant 3 trees with a single tile spacing, then have a 2-tile gap, then another 3 trees.  Using this pattern, one can fit a total of 13 trees, with 1 tiles of width to spare, in a 3x32 Greenhouse, compared to only 10 trees (and 2 spare tiles of width) if they are planted all at a 2-block spacing.  Note that all 3 Arbor Trees must be planted at the same time, as the game will not permit an Arbor Tree seed to be selected for planting unless the entire 3x3 branch area is clear (once planting is queued, obstacles can be placed in the area without issue, as long as they don't block the trunk).
Both the main trunk of the Arbor Tree and its branches can be boosted by Farmer's Touch. Each branch requires a separate application. 


=== Wild ===
A wild Arbor Tree takes 18 cycles to grow, and another 18 cycles to grow a set of branches.
A wild Arbor Tree can produce a maximum of 83.33 kg of wood per cycle or 138.88 g/s (harvested by a duplicant).
A wild Arbor Tree drops a maximum of 39.47 kg of wood per cycle or 65.79 g/s (unharvested).
One Ethanol Distiller can process 7.2 wild trees, and a full ranch of Pips can be supplied by 2.6 (where .2 trees = 1 branch).


=== Domestic ===
Arbor Tree can be planted in a Planter Box, a Farm Tile or a Hydroponic Farm. It needs to be fertilized with 10 kg/cycle of Dirt, and 70 kg/cycle Polluted Water irrigation.
A domestic Arbor Tree takes 4.5 cycles to grow to maturity, and another 4.5 cycles to grow a set of branches.
A domestic Arbor Tree can produce a maximum 333.33 kg of wood per cycle or 555.55 g/s.  This means each Arbor Tree can run 0.56 Ethanol Distillers (ie. 1.8 trees per distillery)
A domestic Arbor Tree that goes through an Ethanol Distiller converts 1kg of Polluted Water into 2.4kg of Ethanol. A Petroleum Generator converts Ethanol at 37.5% Ratio, or 2.4kg of Ethanol into 0.9kg of Polluted Water. 
Each domestic Arbor Tree can feed 12.3 adult Pips (if tame and happy). A maximum-size Stable only needs 0.65 trees, which leaves an average of 116.66kg/cycle (or 194.44g/s) of excess wood, enough to run about 1/5 of an  Ethanol Distiller.


== Decor ==
An Arbor Tree has a decor value of 15 with 2 tiles radius. It applies to the main trunk and each existing branch, which might add up to the value of 90. Which might be convenient for park and nature reserve rooms. However, rooms do not count each branch as an individual plant for the purposes of determining park and nature reserve rooms.


== Heat Economy ==
The branches are spawned at fixed temperature of 20 °C / 68 °F, due to being made out of Genetic Ooze. Harvested Wood spawns at the current temperature of the branch. Branches retain their temperatures between harvests.
Arbor trees produce enough mass to make them heat multiplying if fertilizers are not fed at certain temperatures. It is also beneficial to keep the plant's branches as cold as possible.
The HTC output/input ratio is an enormous ~3.8.
Assuming the branches are kept at 16 °C / 60.8 °F:

If both fertilizers are at 20 °C / 68 °F Arbor trees will produce 20.6 kDTU/s of energy.
Arbor trees become net heat negative if fed water above 62 °C / 143.6 °F and 30 °C / 86 °F dirt.
With 110 °C / 230 °F water and 30 °C / 86 °F dirt one Arbor Tree destroys 23.5 kDTU/s.
If the resulting Wood were to be heated to 70 °C / 158 °F before being consumed, one Arbor Tree would destroy an additional 104 kDTU/s of heat. The Ethanol Distillery produces Ethanol at a minimum temperature of 73.4 °C / 164.12 °F, so heating Wood to this temperature destroys heat. Heating Wood above this temperature increases the temperature of the Ethanol, but the HTC of the Wood is much higher than the Ethanol, so still destroys additional heat.
As a practical matter, Wood has low Thermal Conductivity and is consumed quite rapidly, so rather long heat exchangers are required to get significant heat exchange, hence only a small fraction of that potential is likely to be realized.


== Tips ==
Branches can be  auto-harvested with Waterfalls.
Arbor Acorn can be produced at a much faster rate by  submerging branches in liquids. A Pip must be able to access the tree trunk in order to rummage for any Acorns.


== Database ==
Arbor Tree
Wood Tree

Arbor Trees have been cultivated to spread horizontally when they grow so as to produce a high yield of lumber in vertically cramped spaces.Arbor Trees are related to the oak tree, specifically the Japanese Evergreen, though they have been genetically hybridized significantly.Despite having many hardy, evenly spaced branches, the short stature of the Arbor Tree makes climbing it rather irrelevant.

LU-353289: Arbor trees cannot grow more than 5 branches at once. Irrigation has been changed to polluted water, fertilizer changed from phosphorite into dirt.
LU-358820: Arbor tree branches now have a chance to produce a seed on uproot and harvest.
AP-417040: Fixed the Arbor Tree incorrectly stating that it had a seed drop chance. Pips must be utilized to get extra Arbor Seeds.

Balm Lily is a plant that thrives in the Caustic Biome. It produces 2 Balm Lily Flowers every harvest.


== Seed ==
Balm Lily Seed can be obtained by harvesting and uprooting Balm Lily, or by digging up a Buried Object within the Jungle Biome. It grows into Balm Lily when planted.


== Usage ==
The Balm Lily's flower has great medicinal properties that can be used to make Medical Packs in the Apothecary.
The regular Drecko can eat Balm Lilies, which make them useful as a food source when ranching them, since the plants are maintenance free once the proper atmosphere is set up. However, Glossy Dreckos cannot eat Lilies.
Excess of Balm Lily Flowers can be composted into free dirt:

1 unit of Flowers turns into 1 kilogram of Dirt.
It amounts to 166 g/cycle of Dirt with domesticated Lilies.


== Growth ==
Balm Lily requires an atmosphere of Chlorine, a temperature range of 35 °C ↔ 85 °C / 95 °F ↔ 185 °F, and an air pressure of 150 g - 10 kg.


=== Wild ===
A wild Balm Lily takes 48 cycles to grow.


=== Domestic ===
A Balm Lily can be planted in a Planter Box, Farm Tile or Hydroponic Farm and takes 12 cycles to grow.


== Decor ==
A Balm Lily has a decor value of +15 within 2 tiles.


== Database ==
Balm Lily
Medicinal Herb

The Balm Lily naturally contains high vitamin concentrations and produces acids similar in molecular makeup to acetylsalicylic acid (commonly known as aspirin).As a result, the plant is ideal both for boosting immune systems and treating a variety of common maladies such as pain and fever.


== Tips ==

In Spaced Out!, Balm Lilies can have a Licey mutation causing them to grow food for zero resources, though the presence of radiation will be required.

Bammoths are large critters found in the Cool Pool Biome that consume ethanol-derived plants like Plume Squash, Nosh Bean, and Squash Fries. They excrete Bammoth Patty which can be crushed into Clay and Phosphorite and can be sheared for Reed Fiber. Bammoths drop large amounts of Meat on death.


== Critter Morphs ==
Bammoths which consume Squash Fries increases the chance of laying a Regal Bammoth egg.


=== Bammoth ===
After eating, their fur grows which can be sheared for Reed Fiber. Bammoths has an initial chance of laying Bammoth eggs of 100%, and an initial chance of laying Regal Bammoth eggs of 0%.
 →  →  


=== Regal Bammoth ===
 →  →  
After eating Squash Fries, their crest grows which can be sheared for a Regal Bammoth Crest. The crest can be further crushed at a Rock Crusher for 250kg of Gold Amalgam. Regal Bammoths has an initial chance of laying Bammoth eggs of 2%, and an initial chance of laying Regal Bammoth eggs of 98%.


== Behavior ==
As a large critter, bammoths exhibit unique pathing behavior.

They require 2-tile height pathways
They cannot jump across gaps
They can only jump to 2-tile wide platforms.

In this diagram, the Bammoths can path to Dry Wall marked in blue, but not in red.


== Diet ==
Each satisfied bammoth requires either 4 domestic Plume Squash Plant, about 2.98 domestic Nosh Sprout if eating the plant directly, 2.83 domestic Nosh Sprout if fed harvested Nosh Bean, or Squash Fries. The Squash Fries can be produced from 2.25 domestic Plume Squash Plant  and Tallow from 0.0333 Spigot Seals. Wild plants can be used, multiplying the total number of plants needed by 4. Bammoths may either graze on the plant or be fed Plume Squash/Nosh Bean directly, excreting 30 kg of Bammoth Patty every cycle. For each 1 kg of bammoth patty excreted, 1000 Floral Scent germs are emitted at the patty's location. Having bammoths graze on Plume Squash Plant poses unique challenges in space requirements. The large amount of space allocated for Plume Squash Plant can easily exceed the personal space requirement for a bammoth (16 tiles), resulting in stables with not enough plants for the maximum number of critters.
Bammoth Patty can be crushed at a Rock Crusher to produce about 73.3% Clay and about 26.7% Phosphorite. A satisfied bammoth produces 22 kg of Clay and 8 kg of Phosphorite per cycle after crushing.
Note that feeding Bammoths Nosh Bean directly gives slightly more calories versus letting them graze on Nosh Sprout.


== Thermoregulation ==
Bammoths spawn at 50 °C / 122 °F and will continuously produce 1.3 kDTU/s. Bammoth's thick insulation also makes them impossible to cool down in the presence of elements with low Thermal Conductivity such as Oxygen, Carbon Dioxide, Chlorine, or Vacuum, eventually making them overheat, resulting in -1 happiness.
Furthermore, the Bammoth Patty it excretes is based off its body temperature. Care should be taken when keeping bammoths in the same room as Plume Squash Plant/Nosh Sprout. Both plants' temperature range are below a Bammoth's comfortable range, and Nosh Sprout requires Carbon Dioxide to grow which is not sufficient for keeping Bammoths cool. Moreover, Bammoth patties, excess bammoths, and grazing bammoths all contribute to hotter stables. Promptly sweeping patties, pruning excess bammoths, and cooling through a Thermo Aquatuner is advised to ensure the plants remain the correct temperatures.
Strategies 

A gas like oxygen, even when extremely cold, can only remove about 30% of the internal heat generation, though this will increase the time it takes the bammoth to overheat. Hydrogen is more difficult to work with but much more effective providing 7x more heat exchange than with oxygen.
A very practical way to cool bammoths is using a thin layer of any liquid, which will provide 25x more heat exchange than with oxygen, for example bammoths may be provided with a "wallowing pit" at one end of their ranch.
Rather than trying to manage temperatures it may be easier to simply use a Critter Condo to compensate for the reduced happiness, if the bammoth is allowed to heat up without limit its temperature can exceed their survivable temperature of 100 °C / 212 °F, this won't harm the bammoth (only external temperatures are harmful), but as a caveat the bammoth patties will be equally hot.
Feeding bammoths harvested plume squash or nosh beans saves the need to manage the temperature of crops and bammoths in the same room.
Target Temperature Range for Common Gases/Liquids

Formula for temperature difference at equilibrium: ΔT=1300×0.02517.5×min(kenvironment,0.6) (see Body Temperature#Environmental Exchange)


== Shearing ==
Bammoths grow furry scales at a rate of 10%/cycle while under the effects of "Just Ate". The duration of "Just Ate" is directly proportional to how many calories it consumed in that sitting. A well-fed, satisfied Bammoth will always be under the effects of "Just Ate", while a well-fed glum bammoth will be under the effects of "Just Ate" for 1 cycle out of 5. Once their scale growth reaches 100%, it can be sheared at a Shearing Station to produce 5 units of Reed Fiber. Note that Bammoths scale growth starts at 25% instead of 100%. Regal Bammoths behave similarly, with the added restriction that they must eat Squash Fries to grow their crest ("Regal Fed").


== Food economy ==
With a reproduction rate of 1 egg every 12 cycles, a Bammoth could reasonably lay 15 eggs over its 200 cycle lifecycle. As a Bammoth drops 22400 kcal of meat on death, a Bammoth produces about 1680 (2100 Barbeque, 2730 Pemmican) kcal per cycle.
Plume Squash is roughly converted to Meat at 97% calorie efficiency. (adult Bammoths consume 1778 kcal/cycle of Plume Squash)
Nosh Beans aren't directly edible. Nonetheless, if a generous caloric value of 833 kcal per bean is used by comparing against Nosh Noms, then consuming Nosh Beans yields a calorie efficiency of 124.8%. (adult Bammoths consume 1.616 Nosh Beans/cycle)
Squash Fries are also efficient for converting calories, but requires labor to harvest Plume Squash as well as Tallow to cook into Squash Fries. They also force new eggs to mostly be Regal Bammoths, which can be considered a downside for those seeking Reed Fiber. Squash Fries yields a calorie efficiency of 124.4%. (adult Bammoths consume 1350 kcal/cycle of Squash Fries)
A similar critter are Hatches, which can convert foodstuff to Meat. Hatches have a much more flexible diet, but suffer from a much lower calorie efficiency (72%) and does not offer any additional output besides Meat and Coal. As large critters, Bammoths also produces a lot more meat per unit which can be important for players trying to minimize critter count and dupe labor.
In term of Ethanol-to-Food efficiency, feeding Plume Squash converts 60 kg of Ethanol to 1680 kcal of Meat per cycle (28 kcal per kg of Ethanol), and feeding Squash Fries converts 33.75 kg of Ethanol to 1680 kcal of Meat per cycle (49.8 kcal per kg of Ethanol).

Bammoth
Domesticable Critter

The Bammoth is one of the oldest species on record, with ancient skeletal remains dating back approximately 10,000 years.This placid herbivore is known for its unique body language: an angry young Bammoth expresses displeasure by flopping down dramatically in front of its opponent, while older creatures with limited mobility will sit facing away from the source of their annoyance.Licking the ground in front of a caregiver can be a sign of either deep affection or mineral deficiency.

Beetas are Critters that live close to Beeta Hives in the Radioactive Biome. They can be pacified by filling their room with Carbon Dioxide so they fall asleep. Their lifespan is very limited at the age of five cycles, but the hive provides a replacement every cycle.
When not asleep, Beetas sting duplicants and die shortly after, similar to real life social bees. On death, a Beeta drops 1000 g of Nuclear Waste as a supercooled liquid.


=== Beetiny ===
A Beetiny is the larval stage of a Beeta. This creature crawls near the hive, being unable to jump up or down one tile and unable to attack. Upon reaching age two, it turns into a Beeta if there is a nearby Beeta Hive. If instead are no accessible Beeta Hives on nightfall, and there is sufficient space for a hive, it turns into a Beeta Hive that matures in three cycles. A Beeta Hive can be formed at any time during the night hours (schedule blocks 22-24), and this means when a Beetiny is relocated to a place that satisfies the conditions during these hours, it will immediately form a Beeta Hive.
Unlike the mature Beeta, Beetinys are wranglable.


=== Printerceptor Story Trait ===
Beetiny is the only live creature that can be printed from the Printerceptor, and as such has unique considerations when printing.  Due to the low livable temperature range, the beetiny will die quickly after being printed if the area around the printer is not cooled to sufficient temperatures or wrangled immediately.  Additionally the beetiny must be in a location with enough unoccupied space to form a beeta hive, or it will transform into an adult Beeta instead.


=== Diet and Pacification ===
Beeta flies around gathering Uranium Ore to feed into its hive. The structure then converts Uranium into Enriched Uranium.
When Carbon Dioxide gas is present, Beetas and Beetinys enter a sleeping state and consume it at 100 g/s. This allows for preventing stings when harvesting Enriched Uranium from a Beeta Hive. The critters can be prevented from sleeping by submerging them in a small amount of liquid, allowing them to grow up normally with constant sleeping, and concentrating of Beetas into a nearby sleeping spot for radiation harvesting.


=== Radioactivity ===
Beetas pose a significant radioactive hazard when sleeping, as each Beeta puts out 1440 rads/cycle, while each Beetiny puts out 480 rads/cycle. and Lead Suits are recommended for Duplicants to avoid radiation poisoning.

Beetas are insectoid creatures that enjoy a symbiotic relationship with the radioactive environment they thrive in.Much like the honey bee gathers nectar and processes it to honey, the Beeta turns Uranium Ore into Enriched Uranium through a complex process of isotope separation inside the Beeta Hive.When first observing the Beeta's enrichment process, many scientists note with surprise just how much more efficient the cooperative combination of insect and hive is when compared to even the most advanced industrial processes.

Bog Buckets are a Food Plant which can be found in the Swampy Biome. It can be grown by planting a Bog Bucket Seed and produces Bog Jelly.


== Seed ==
Bog Bucket Seed can be obtained by harvesting and uprooting Bog Bucket, or by digging up a Buried Object within the Swampy Biome. It grows into Bog Bucket when planted.


== Food ==
It produces 1840 kcals Bog Jelly per harvest every 6.6 cycles, which can be eaten raw (Terrible Food Quality) or be further cooked into Swampy Delights with no extra resource requirement.
Swampy Delights has a Poor (+1) food quality and provides 2240 kcals from 1840 kcals of Bog Jelly cooked at the grill. Cooking at the grill will also remove food poisoning germs if they were present in the polluted water used to irrigate the Bog Bucket plants.
Uncooked, to feed one Duplicant you need 3.6 Bog Buckets, For a crew of 8 Dupes, that's 29 Bog Buckets, requiring 1160 kg Polluted Water per cycle.
Cooked, to feed one Duplicant you need 2.95 Bog Buckets. For a crew of 8 Dupes, that's 24 Bog Buckets, requiring 960 kg Polluted Water per cycle.


=== Notes ===
Bog Buckets are the only food plant which consumes Polluted Water and can be grown in a Planter Box instead of an Hydroponic Farm. This allows them to serve as a convenient early-game sink for the bottled polluted water generated by Wash Basins and Algae Terraria.


== Database ==

Bog Buckets get their name from their bucket-like flowers and their propensity to grow in swampy, bog-like environments.The flower secretes a thick, sweet liquid which collects at the bottom of the bucket and can be gathered for consumption.Though not inherently dangerous, the interior of the Bog Bucket flower is so warm and inviting that it has tempted individuals to climb inside for a nap, only to awake trapped in its sticky sap.

Bonbon Tree is a Plant that can live in Vacuum or cold environment and is found naturally in Nectar Biome. It grows up to 5 branches from its trunk, which produce Nectar when exposed to Light. The branches can be harvested for Wood; however, that will temporarily disrupt the nectar production. The nectar can be harvested from the trunk by a Duplicant skilled with (Crop Tending) or directly with pipes.


== Seed ==
The Bonbon Tree Seed is the seed of a Bonbon Tree. As the tree itself does not have harvestable items, it can not directly produce new Bonbon Tree Seeds like traditional plants.
However, additional seeds can be obtained through a variety of methods:

Uprooting an Bonbon Tree - in addition to the ones found in the Nectar Biome, Bonbon Meteor from the Icy Nectar Meteor Showers also self-plants a Bonbon Tree at its impact.
Bonbon Tree Seeds can be obtained from Care Packages after Cycle 24.
Spigot Seals have a 20% chance of dropping a Bonbon Tree Seed whenever they poop.


== Growth ==
It takes 4.5 cycles (18 cycles if wild) for the trunk to mature, and an additional 4.5 cycles (18 cycles if wild) for each branch to mature. A Bonbon Tree branch additionally requires at least 300 Lux to grow. Unlike most plants, Bonbon Trees and its branches will never grow old and self-harvest.
While the farmer's touch bonus from a Farm Station improves the rate of trunk and branch growth, it does not affect nectar production.


== Usage ==
Bonbon Trees produces Nectar directly into its trunk, depending on the health of its branches. Each non-wilting Bonbon Tree Branch produces 16 kg/cycle of Nectar when Lux exceeds 10000. If Lux is less than 10000, then nectar production is reduced proportional to the Lux level, with a minimum of 300 Lux. (1000 Lux would only produce 1.6 kg/cycle of Nectar)
Spigot Seals can drink the Nectar directly from a Bonbon Tree.
Pips can eat Bonbon Tree branches. Unlike Arbor Tree branches, the branches need to be fully mature before a Pip will eat it.
Harvesting the branches from the Bonbon Tree yields 75 kg of Wood. Comparing to Arbor Trees, this is 4 times less productive than an Arbor Tree.


== Branch Placement ==

Drecko is a critter found in the Caustic Biome. They are a renewable source of Phosphorite, which makes them important for Wheezeworts maintenance and Fertilizer production. == Behavior ==
This creature can be found crawling around in cavities in the Caustic Biome. They are able to cling strongly to any surface, and will freely wander the full perimeter of whatever chamber they are in. They are not hostile and are quite mobile, inevitably wandering away from any chamber they are not trapped in.  
It will fight back when attacked, but is no match for even an unskilled Duplicant. It drops 3200 kcal (2 kg) of Meat on death. 
Regular Dreckos and Glossy Drecko both have a default bodily temperature of 35 °C / 95 °F at birth. They will slowly come to match the environmental temperature with time. Caution in temperature regulation needs to be taken when ranching Dreckos in a Mealwood farm in a perfectly insulated environment, especially if supplying Mealwood with hot Dirt . This can gradually heat the farm to above 30 °C / 86 °F, halting Mealwood growth.


== Feeding ==
Unlike other critters, they consume the growing plant and reduce its growth percentage, including being able to consume "harvest ready" plants. They can only feed on plants with a minimum growth of 25%. They can eat directly from Farm Tiles/Hydroponic Farms/Planter Boxes. It may be worthwhile to disable "Auto-Harvest" on plants for players with no intention of using Balm Lily or consuming Mealwood. Fully fed tame Dreckos have 10,000 kcal available to them and considering their Metabolism remains 100% they will lose 2000 calories each cycle. After reaching 9000 calories or less they will start looking for food and once they find it they will eat until full. Under perfect conditions Dreckos will attempt to feed twice a cycle.
Tame Dreckos feeding on domesticated plants will consume 75% (100% for Glossy Drecko) of the plants growth each cycle, meaning the growth rate % taken away from the plant each time they feed is relative to the plant they are consuming. As an example Balm Lily grows 8.33% each cycle and a regular Drecko will drain 75% of this value (6.25%). Note that Metabolism will only stay at 100% while the grooming effect is active so these numbers will never translate perfectly to actual gameplay.


== Breeding ==
Drecko eggs have a base incubation rate of 3.33% per cycle. When put in a powered incubator, their incubating rate is increased to 16.67%. An incubated Drecklet will mature into a Drecko after 5 cycles.


== Variants ==
The Drecko has two variants, each with its own varied diet preferences. Along with the plain Drecko, there is also the Glossy Drecko. When baby Dreckos mature to adult Dreckos, their Scale Growth resets to 90%. (This does not occur for Glossy Dreckos)

A Drecko fed primarily Mealwood will have a chance of producing a Glossy Drecko Egg, with a larger chance given a higher volume of Mealwood consumed. The Glossy Drecko shares the same behavior of the Drecko, but when sheared produces Plastic instead of Reed Fiber, along with being incapable of eating anything but Mealwood & Bristle Blossom.


== Drecko Ranching ==
Drecko are finicky critters to domesticate in a fully productive way, due to their mixed environment preferences. They live 150 cycles, but reproduce fairly slowly. They need access to growing Pincha Pepper, Balm Lily or Mealwood plant to satisfy their dietary requirements and produce Phosphorite.  The ratio for Plants to Drecko is 3 Plants to 4 Drecko and 1 Plant to 1 Glossy Drecko with their respective diet. Using wild instead of domesticated plants, the ratio increases to 3 Plants to 1 Drecko and 4 Plants to 1 Glossy Drecko. They only produce Reed Fiber or Plastic when in a Hydrogen atmosphere. When tame they regenerate their "wool" at a rate that allows harvest once roughly every 8 cycles for Drecko or 3 cycles for Glossy Drecko, provided they are completely immersed in hydrogen for the entire duration.


=== Reed Fiber farm ===
The goal of this setup is to produce Reed Fiber with plain Drecko. This is quite helpful in Arboria Asteroid and The Badlands Asteroid where Swamp Biome is missing.
Build a stable room of three layers. The bottom layer is filled with Chlorine to grow Balm Lily, as it does not require maintenance once planted. The middle layer is filled with Oxygen for Duplicants' convenience to work with  the Grooming Station and Shearing Station. The top layer is filled with Hydrogen for Dreckos to grow Reed Fiber scales. With this setup, Dreckos can eat Balm Lily in the bottom layer, and grow Reed Fiber scale when they move to the top layer. Duplicants can tame the Drecko and shear the scales in the middle layer.
It also possible to completely seal the room with a liquid lock and provide Atmo Suit access, in which case an oxygen layer is not necessary. This also means the Dreckos spend potentially more time in hydrogen.
Alternatively, Pincha Pepper can be grown in a room completely flooded with hydrogen. It requires Phosphorite for fertilization, which the Dreckos supply. However, it also needs a constant supply of polluted water. 
Either plant may require some initial heating of the atmosphere in order to satisfy their temperature requirement. It is thus best to build the outer walls out of Insulated Tile.


=== Plastic farm ===
The goal of this setup is to produce Plastic with Glossy Drecko. Compared with Polymer Press, this approach is more energy efficient and produces less heat. It can also be achieved relatively early, long before access to the Oil Biome.
Build a room with hydrogen on top and oxygen at the bottom. Grow roughly a dozen Mealwood plants in the oxygen, which also allows a ranching Dupe to breathe. Starting with regular Drecko, the Mealwood diet ensures that they eventually lay Glossy Drecko eggs. Regular Drecko may later be moved to their own specialized stable.
To create the required atmosphere, hydrogen can be released at the bottom of the base and allowed to drift upwards into the Drecko stable. To supply a more measured amount without gas piping, the Canister Filler and Emptier may be used to transport hydrogen from far away. Enough hydrogen supplied this way will ensure a stable top layer even at maximum oxygen pressure from below. A completely sealed room is thus not required.
An Incubator can be placed in the hydrogen layer and cooled with a Wheezewort next to it if the temperature it gives off threatens the Mealwood growth.
A half dozen Glossy Drecko will produce roughly 1 ton of Plastic every 10 cycles with such a setup, along with several tons of Phosphorite and multiple eggs. This can be a sustainable alternative in obtaining plastic in the mid to late game.
The excess of plastic produced this way can also be converted into Naphtha by melting  it, or Natural Gas by melting and re-cooling at the later stages of the game. One stable of Glossy Drecko can produce ~250 kg plastic/cycle if sheared regularly. It would be enough to power 3 Natural Gas Generators with 100% uptime (2.4 kW of power).


=== Phosphorite farm ===
If the shearing is not a priority the setup can be simplified to a chlorine pit with domesticated Balm Lilies, where all wild Dreckos get dumped. The maps usually have enough of them to generate abundant stream of phosphorite.


=== Auto-surplus method ===
Another method of farming Plastic  without a hydrogen filled-room is to make use of the auto-surplus wrangling and Incubator system. Since newborn baby Glossy Dreckos grow up with 100% scale growth, they can be sheared as soon as they become adults and then moved to another location for culling with the auto-surplus function. This does not work with normal Dreckos.
A 96 tiles room will have a limit of 8 dreckos including egg count before the crowded penalty kicks in.
This setup can benefit from automation with timers for scheduling and Drowning chamber to free up duplicants from mass slaughter.


=== Shearing excess dreckos in overflow room(s) ===
Since Dreckos don't require food and only Glum mood for their scales to grow, you can dump excess dreckos in overflow rooms filled with Hydrogen rather than eagerly drowning baby Dreckos or cracking their eggs. They will go longer without starving if they are not groomed due to the metabolism penalty. They will reach an age of 27.5 cycles before starving, in which you can shave Dreckos 3 times and the glossy variant 8 times. 
This method is not sustainable without an additional source of Drecko eggs, and care must be taken to ensure the dreckos are not miserable from Crowded as that will also halt their scale growth.

Although the Gas Grass does not require a specific atmosphere to grow, some gases absorb light which can result in the plants not reaching the required illumination. == Farming economy ==
Sustaining the stable population requires the stable to have a tile within view of space for the Gassy Moos to call for others, Liquid Chlorine  , Dirt , and possibly more significant amounts of power in order to produce artificial light for the Gas Grass.
Liquid Chlorine   may be obtained by cooling Chlorine  below it's condensation point (-34.6 °C / -30.28 °F). Despite the low condensation temperature, Chlorine's low specific heat capacity combined with the small amounts needed for Gas Grass makes this a low energy endeavor.
Solid Chlorine  can be obtained from Chlorine Planets.
Liquid Chlorine   can be obtained directly from Radioactive Gas or Chlorine Clouds.
Gas Grass requires 10,000 Lux (Bright) to grow, which can be attained via sunlight, an array of Ceiling Lights directly above the grass, Mercury Ceiling Light, or use of the Sun Lamp. Use of sunlight to grow Gas Grass will result in down-periods during the night, as 0 lux will halt the Gas Grass from growing. In addition, since space with sunlight is limited to the width of the world, sunlight Gassy Moo stables indirectly competes with Solar Panels for space.
Alternatively, natural sunlight can be supplemented with a Sun Lamp controlled with a Light Sensor to allow Gas Grass to grow at all times while minimizing the power consumption.

The Hatch is a Critter found in the starting Temperate Biome. They produce Coal, Eggs, Meat, and Refined Metal. They can be domesticated.


== Behavior ==
This creature is nocturnal and eats minerals in its path. It burrows into natural tiles with a hardness of 20 or lower to hide for the day time, and the tile in which it's burrowed can be dug up to encounter the creature. These DO include natural tiles with "buried object" in them and are surrounded on all sides by other natural tiles. 
If there are few surface hatches in the Sandstone starting biome, simply excavate to quickly encounter more. On most asteroid types without the starting Sandstone Biome (such as Verdante, Arboria, and Aridio), there is a single buried Hatch near the Printing Pod.
The Hatch drops 3200 kcal (2 kg) of Meat on death.
Hatches convert a certain percentage of the eaten mass into another resource (e.g. regular Hatches eat 140 kg of solids and convert them into 70 kg of coal). 
Note that regular Hatches and Sage Hatches can also eat food. However, they only eat a few grams of food and thus only convert it into a few grams of coal. Because of this, food is not a good diet if you want your Hatches to provide the Coal for a Coal Generator.


== Critter Morphs ==
Hatches have four critter morphs, each with its own varied diet preferences. Along with the Hatch, two of its morphs provide a greatly diversified diet that may be better tailored to the needs of your colony's coal production. The final variant provides a refining service that is otherwise heat intensive, power hungry and time consuming.
Hatches which consume Dirt  improve their chance of laying a Sage Hatch. Hatches which consume Sedimentary Rock  improve their chance of laying a Stone Hatch. Hatches which consume certain types of metal ore improve their chance of laying a Smooth Hatch. For exact details, see Critter Morphs.


=== Hatch ===
 →  →  
The Hatch that is the purple, toothy critter your Duplicants seem to stumble upon in their initial excavations. It eats a wide variety of the same foodstuffs your duplicants subsist on, along with some minerals, and produces coal in return. It provides a minor decor bonus (+10) in its immediate radius. If fed Sedimentary Rock, it has an increased chance of producing a Stone Hatchling Egg. If fed Dirt, it has an increased chance of producing a Sage Hatchling Egg. When killed it provides 2000 g of meat.


=== Sage Hatch ===
 →  →  
Sage Hatches have a glossy green color, and a green diet to match. It consumes almost exclusively organic compounds, including Polluted Dirt, slime, and algae, alongside every normal foodstuff your dupes eat such as Meal Lice. It produces coal in return. It is completely indifferent to bacteria or spoilage, and effectively consumes otherwise spoiled, inedible or over abundant organics your dupes can't use.
Sage Hatches have the highest conversion rate among all four variants. It can convert 100% consumed mass into Coal.
Sage Hatches are more efficient than Normal or Stone Hatches for coal production, as they convert 100% of the consumed mass into Coal, thus needing half as many per Coal Generator. However, a conventional colony might find it difficult to acquire enough Dirt to fulfill their hunger. One of the most common means to address this is to use an Ethanol Distiller.  Algae can be produced in vast quantities through Blum Lumbs. As well as, when attempting the Carnivore or Locavore Achievements, Sage Hatches can be a way to make use of otherwise useless Dirt and Fertilizer.


=== Stone Hatch ===
 →  → 
Stone Hatches are flinty grey and have a thickened, rocky appearance. They consume primarily mineral materials such as Igneous Rock. They also consume some Raw Metals, such as Copper Ore or Iron Ore, producing an equal volume of coal in exchange. 
If fed Copper Ore, Gold Amalgam, Iron Ore, or Wolframite the Stone Hatch has an increased chance of producing a Smooth Hatch egg.
This variation is considerably tougher than normal Hatch, with more hp and attack, and caution should be used when attempting to kill it as it could severely injure or kill a lone dupe.

It is wise to consider wrangling them before killing them. No critter can break out of wrangling, not even these, and wrangled critters will not break free if they are shot at either.


=== Smooth Hatch ===
 →  → 
Smooth Hatches are a deep cobalt blue. They eat metal ore exclusively, and instead of producing coal, they produce Refined Metal of the corresponding ore instead. They will eat a 100 kg of ore, "refining" it into 75 kg of Refined Metal. The Smooth Hatch is even tougher than the Stone Hatch, with double the hitpoints and thus are dangerous to fight alone should you order your dupes to attack one.


== Tips ==


=== Hatch Farming for Meat and Eggs ===
Duplicants require 1000 kcal per cycle on normal difficulty settings (default). A hatch provides 2 kg of meat on death, which is 3200 kcal of food directly, or 4000 if cooked into barbecue.
Hatches spend 5 cycles out of their 100-cycle lifespan as unproductive babies, so happy hatches can lay up to 15 eggs over their entire adult life (95 cycles), one of which must be used to replace the hatch when it dies of old age. This is 30 kg of meat over 100 cycles, or 480 kcal/cycle in meat (600 kcal/cycle barbecue), meaning ~2.08 (~1.66) hatches are required to feed one dupe. Optimizing the ranches manually by removing Hatches that won't be able to lay an egg before they die, and replacing them with the youngest adult Hatch, can provide a mild increase to meat output.  The approximate maximum that can be achieved with this is the raw breeding rate, ie. 2 kg of meat every 6 cycles.  This tallies up to about 533 kcals/cycle of meat, or 667 kcals/cycle barbecue, requiring only 1.5 hatches per dupe if perfectly optimized, which can make the Carnivore achievement easier to acquire. These ideal rates are not easily attained so it's good to oversize your ranching population slightly to account for inefficiencies and downtime, such as from unavailable Duplicant labor or the cramped debuff slowing reproduction rates until eggs are removed from the stable.
The 14 eggs not used for replacing the hatch may instead be cracked into Omelettes. Hatch eggs crack into 1600 kcals of Raw Egg, which then cook into 2800 kcals of Omelettes, so 14 eggs is 39,200 kcals of Omelettes, plus 4000 kcals of barbecue from the Hatch laying the eggs, for a total of 43,200 kcals of food per 100 cycles, or 432 kcal/cycle.  This is dramatically inferior (35% lower, to be precise) to kcal output of the pure barbecue route, along with Omelettes being 1 food quality tier lower and requiring an additional cooking appliance.  On the other hand, the pure Barbeque route requires waiting for the hatches to hatch from their eggs, and a drowning chamber or other method for slaughtering the extra hatches.
When combined with a Pacu tank, and once the Gas Range is researched, built, and supplied, the barbecue from the Hatches and the Cooked Seafood from the Pacu can be combined into Surf'n'Turf, further increasing the calorie count by a small amount, as well as yielding an additional food quality tier over barbecue and cooked seafood.  When fed this way, each dupe requires 1 Hatch and 0.25 pacu, if perfectly optimized.


=== Hatch Coal Herding ===
The goal of setting up this kind of herding operation is to have (Stone) Hatches producing coal at a rapid rate. Each Coal Generator consumes 600 kg of Coal a Cycle when running constantly. You need 8.5 tame and happy (Stone) Hatches to produce 600 kg of coal each cycle. You can fit at most 8 Hatches in one Stable, so technically you would need more than one stable to fuel one coal generator constantly. However, usually coal generators don't need to run all the time so your actual requirements may be less.
If there is a Volcano on the map and its Magma is cooled down into Igneous Rock, feeding it to Stone Hatches provides a renewable way to produce coal.


=== Hatch Garbage Disposal Herding ===
Sage Hatches will eat spoiled, over-abundant, bacteria-laced, or other undesirable food like Mealwood and Plant Meat as well as unwanted organics like Slime and Polluted Dirt. They make for delicious Barbeque or a consistent stream of eggs (once every 6 cycles). Sage hatches convert roughly 90.2% of the calories it consumes into eventual BBQ.


=== Hatch Refinery Herding ===
Smooth Hatches refine metals more efficiently than a Rock Crusher, but less so than a Metal Refinery. While it takes some investment to breed a Smooth Hatch, once obtained they can provide a reliable source of refined metal without needing power and without producing large amounts of heat. Careful estimation of just how much refined metal should be made and the number of Hatch should be carefully managed unless you wish to find yourself running out of ore. 3 - 4 Smooth Hatches can produce enough refined metal for most early - mid game needs. They continue producing eggs like other Hatch sub-species, though caution must be exercised when harvesting full grown Smooth Hatch for meat - they can incapacitate a lone unskilled dupe easily. As such, if Smooth Hatches are also ranched for meat, use of a Drowning chamber is recommended.

 All Shine Bugs give off Radiation, 60 Rads at the tile they occupy, with a radius of 6 tiles (including the central tile.) There is no difference in the amount of radiation given off by the different Shine Bug morphs.


== Behavior ==
Shine Bugs are relatively rare, with two or three spawning in the temperate biome. They are commonly found in places with lots of Mealwood, Bristle Blossoms, Bluff Briars, and Muckroots. They can drown in water and can be killed by attacking them.
Shine Bugs are quite lonely critters, as only a few exist in the asteroid, so they constantly seek each other, and sometimes mistake Duplicant-made lighting as new friends, bobbing up and down in greeting. They are, however, attracted to things emitting light, and are more likely to move towards things such as lamps, light bulbs, or other Shine Bugs. Shine bugs will consume any Gristle Berry or Bristle Berry that is found lying around. They seem oblivious to the atmosphere in which they're kept, although temperature extremes will prove lethal to them.


== Critter Morphs ==
Shine bugs enjoy the largest array of critter morphs that can be unlocked through Ranching, each critter morph requiring a different foodstuff and providing a progressively increased decor benefit. They must be raised successively, with each generation providing a chance to produce the next when provided with the correct foodstuff.
They are as follows:


=== Shine Bug ===
 →  → 
The original variant consumes Bristle Berry, Gristle Berry and Phosphorite. They provide illumination and moderately improve decor (+30) in a modest 5 tile radius. They are short lived, but reproduce quickly with a 67% per cycle reproduction rate when tamed and fed. If fed Gristle Berry, they have an increased chance of producing Sun Nymph eggs.
Shine Bugs emit light at 1800 Lux while uncrowded.


=== Sun Bug ===
 →  → 
The second possible variant, Sun Bugs are orange in coloration and continue providing illumination and a high decor bonus (+50), as well as increase its radius to 7 tiles. They eat Fried Mushroom, Gristle Berry, Mushroom, and Phosphorite. If fed Fried Mushroom, they have an increased chance of producing Royal Nymph Eggs.
Sun Bugs emit light at 1800 Lux while uncrowded.


=== Royal Bug ===
 →  → 
The third variant, Royal Bugs are a royal purple and provide the same decor bonus as Sun Bug. They eat Fried Mushroom, Gristle Berry, Pepper Bread, Phosphorite, and Pincha Peppernut. If fed Pepper Bread, they have an increased chance of producing Coral Nymph Eggs.


=== Coral Bug ===
 →  → 
The fourth variant, Coral Bugs are a pink hue and provide the same decor value and radius as Royal Bug. They eat Bristle Berry, Fried Mushroom, Gristle Berry, Pepper Bread, Phosphorite, and Stuffed Berry. If fed Stuffed Berry they have an increased chance of producing Azure Nymph Eggs.


=== Azure Bug ===
 →  → 
The fifth variant, Azure Bugs are a dark blue hue and the same decor value and radius as the Coral Bug. They eat Pepper Bread, Phosphorite, Refined Phosphorus, and Stuffed Berry. If fed Refined Phosphorus, they have an increased chance of producing Abyss Nymph eggs.


=== Abyss Bug ===
 →  → 
The sixth variant, Abyss Bugs are a translucent black hue. They have a very high decor value (+80) with a 7 tile radius, but no longer produce light, which by itself would provide a decor value of +15. They live considerably longer than previous variants, tripling their lifespan to 75 cycles, but also greatly reduce their reproductive rate to 22% per cycle. This means that Abyss Bugs (and Radiant Bugs) will not be able to lay an egg before they die of starvation, if tame but not fed. They eat Abyssalite , Barbeque, Meat, Refined Phosphorus, and Stuffed Berry. If fed Barbeque, they have an increased chance to produce Radiant Nymph eggs.


=== Radiant Bug ===
 →  → 
The seventh and final variant, Radiant Bugs are colorlessly translucent. They have an astoundingly high decor value (+200) with a 8 tile radius, produce light with a 5 tile radius, and keep the extended life and reduced reproduction rates of the Abyss Bug. They eat Barbeque and Diamond . They will almost always produce more Radiant Nymph eggs, with a tiny chance to produce an original Shine Nymph Egg.


== Tips ==


=== Resin Production ===
Shine Bug eggs can be cracked at an Egg Cracker to produce 5 kg of Resin   . Note that eggs deteriorating in storage due to 0% viability do not drop any Resin. On some asteroid starts, this is the earliest way for a player to acquire wood building material which is needed to construct Communal Tables, Hot Tubs, and Saunas.
This is also technically an early source of Plastic , although considerable time and effort is needed to produce enough to construct something useful - if a happy Shine Bug lays 13 eggs in its lifetime and 1 is used for replenishing the stable, then it effectively produces about 2.4 kg/cycle of Resin or 1.4 kg/cycle of Plastic. A full, 16 shine bug stable produces about 23 kg/cycle which is enough to construct a Steam Turbine in 8.68 cycles. For perspective, a single Glossy Drecko can be sheared for 50 kg/cycle and produces enough for a Steam Turbine in 4 cycles.


=== Shine Bug Decor Farming ===
Shine Bug ranches with Window Tiles as ceiling and floor can be placed near areas that would benefit from high Decor, such as Great Hall and Recreational Room, or areas with a large source of Decor penalty (such as Heavi-Watt Wire).
To make the Decor bonus from Shine Bugs more consistent, place a Lamp or a Ceiling Light at one side and a Critter Feeder on the other side.
All variants between Sun Bug and Azure Bug have the same Decor bonus, so the excess of these Shine Bugs can be allowed to roam around the base, as long as they cannot enter areas with extreme temperatures or areas that must be kept dark, such as bedrooms and Dusk Cap farms.
The Abyss Bug variant doesn't emit light, so it can be worthwhile to set up a dedicated ranch for Abyss Bugs to boost Decor in rooms that must be kept dark.


=== Radiant Bug Breeding ===


==== Initial Breeding ====
Shine Bugs reproduce quickly (2 eggs every 3 cycles), so just feeding all Shine Bugs with Phosphorite  allows breeding up to Abyss Bugs in around 50 cycles.
Feeding variants with their respective specialized diet can greatly accelerate this process, but requires more management.
Make sure to remove eggs from the stable to prevent the cramped debuff from slowing down egg production.
It is recommended to keep a separate stable of Abyss Bugs fed off a diet of Abyssalite  before moving on the Radiant Bug variant, in order to boost Decor in places that must be kept dark.


==== Feeding Radiant Bugs ====
Radiant Bugs can eat 1 kg of Diamond  or 1 kg (4000 kcal) of Barbeque per cycle. If both are in short supply, Shove Voles can be ranched for large amounts of meat.
Note that Barbeque production can occupy an Electric Grill for a large amount of time.
To prevent Barbeque spoilage, limit the Critter Feeder storage to 8 kg or lower, or maintain Deep Freeze and Sterile Atmosphere environments.
Alternatively, feed Abyss Bugs with Barbeque temporarily to increase the Radiant Bug Egg chance, then switch back to Abyssalite  to save on Barbeque. This involves considerable user intervention.


==== Distribution and Decor Boost ====
Excess Radiant Bugs can be distributed to places that would benefit from high Decor, as mentioned above. Radiant Bugs can produce exceptionally high Decor compared to other variants.
When Radiant Bugs are distributed in kitchen areas, they may consume fresh Barbeque if it is not stored quickly.


=== Medicine Herding ===
Sun Bugs can be bred to produce Sun Bug Eggs, which can then be used to produce Serum Vial, which cures Zombie Spores.


=== Shine Bug Reactor Farming ===
Create a 3*3 box of Window Tiles, sealing one of the sides with a Liquid Airlock.
Put a Conveyor Chute on the center tile to deliver excess eggs from a breeding ranch. Any variant until Azure Bug can be used for this purpose, to maintain a population without feeding.
Place Solar Panels below and to the sides of this box. In Spaced Out, place Radbolt Generators around to harvest Radiation as Radbolts.
Continuously deliver eggs using the Conveyor Chute. Solar Panels max out at 50-100 Shine Bugs, while Radiation maxes out at 150,000 Shine Bugs.
Note that the overlapping light of the Shine Bugs will render their light radius pure white. In this case, Decor Overlay (F8) or Room Overlay (F11) can be used to check the number of Shine Bugs inside.

Jawbo are carnivorous aquatic critters that feed on Pacus and produce Rust .
They pose no threat to Duplicants.


== Behavior ==
 →  → 
Jawbo  will seek out live Pacu to eat. Unlike Rhex, Jawbo is guaranteed to succeed in eating live prey.  As only the Fish Feeder can make Jawbo happy, this significantly reduces the number of eggs the Jawbo lays.


== Diet ==
A Jawbo consumes 1 unit of Pacu, or  1,000 kcal Fish Fillet every cycle and excretes up to 60 kg/cycle of Rust  . A tamed, happy Pacu can produce about 520 kcal/cycle of Fish Fillet every cycle. Thus, each Jawbo requires about 1.92 Pacu.


== Food economy ==
Happy Jawbos with a baseline happiness of +4 have a reproduction rate of 1 egg every 6 cycles and can reasonably lay 15 eggs in its lifetime. As a Jawbo drops 12,000 kcal of Jawbo Fillet on death, it produces about 1,800 kcal Jawbo Fillet every cycle, which can be turned into 3,360 kcal of Smoked Fish every cycle at the Smoker. Although this seems like a large caloric multiplier, the regular Fish Fillet may also be used in the Smoker. Comparing the fillets directly still puts the Jawbo at a modest, but still sizable 180% (1,000 kcal → 1,800 kcal) conversion rate of Fish Fillet to Jawbo Fillet.
Cooking the Fish Fillet and feeding Cooked Seafood instead improves its happiness by 2, enabling the Jawbo to lay 22 eggs in its lifetime. This improves Jawbo Fillet production to about 2640 kcal/cycle, a 264% conversion ratio from fish fillet. Smoked Fish production increases to 4928 kcal/cycle.


== Notes ==
If a Jawbo hunts a Pacu with more than 400 kcal in its stomach, then the excess calories gets converted into Fish Fillet.
Jawbo will not hunt Pacu if confined into a 1x1 cell.


== Tips ==
When fed to a Rust Deoxidizer, the rust from 1 Jawbo and 20 kg/cycle of Salt becomes 45.6 kg of Oxygen, 32 kg of Iron Ore, and 2.4 kg of Chlorine Gas per cycle. 

If converting Iron Ore to Iron by melting it or using a Metal Refinery, 6 fed Jawbo will produce slightly more Iron than the average Iron Volcano.


== Trivia ==
Jawbo is the second critter in the game that provides a renewable source of Metal Ore, after Regal Bammoth. However, to actually get Iron Ore  or Iron , the player needs a source of Salt  for Rust Deoxidizer, or a source of heat that can melt Rust .

The Blum Lumb is very similar to the Lumb, except that it poops large amounts of Algae  instead of Peat . Algae can be used to produce Oxygen  directly through the Oxygen Diffuser or fed to Pacus. Each tame, satisfied Blumb Lumb produces enough Algae for 120 kg/cycle Oxygen , or 180 kg/cycle when fed with Bog Jelly. This is enough to supply 2 duplicants (or 3 with Bog Jelly).
The Algae can also be used to keep up to 17.6 Pacu fed, or 26.4 Pacu when fed with Bog Jelly.


== Diet ==
Lumbs consume 1,300 kcal kcal/cycle of either Ovagro Fig, Bristle Berry, or Bog Jelly. They do not directly graze from the plant, but their unique harvesting behavior synergizes with growing these plants accessible to Lumbs.


== Food Economy ==
Lumbs do not directly drop edible food. However, its Tough Meat can be cooked at a Smoker to produce 32,000 kcal of food. Happy Lumbs have a reproduction rate of 1 egg every 12 cycles and can reasonably lay 15 eggs in its lifetime. As a Lumb drops 12 kg of Tough Meat on death, it produces about 900 g of Tough Meat every cycle, which can be turned into 2,400 kcal of Tender Brisket every cycle.


== Wild Utility ==
It may be beneficial to keep Wild Lumbs around by intentionally not taming any that spawned on world generation, printing Lumblets from the Printing Pod, or choosing Lumblet Eggs from the Printerceptor. A glum, ungroomed Lumb will starve to death before reproducing which necessitates some feeding, while a Wild Lumb does not require any maintenance given ideal room conditions. Wild Lumbs can be used to harvest crops quickly and without duplicant labor without the overhead of feeding a critter.


== Oxygen Economy ==
Ranching Blum Lumbs, then using the algae produced in an Oxygen Diffuser produces dramatically more oxygen from water than any other method. An Electrolyzer converts 88.8% of the water into oxygen. Letting Polluted Water off-gas and using a Deodorizer to filter the Polluted Oxygen converts 90% of the polluted water into oxygen. 
Feeding 2 Blum Lumbs Ovagro Fig costs 90 kg/cycle of Water, and produces 264 kg/cycle of Algae. Using this algae in an oxygen diffuser produces 240 kg/cycle of oxygen, 267% the mass of the water. Each Blum Lumb produces enough oxygen via this method to fully support 2 dupes under ideal conditions.
This conversion rate makes the oxygen diffuser far more efficient for oxygen than the Algae Terrarium. The oxygen diffuser converts less than 91% the mass of the algae into oxygen, but the algae terrarium expends 5.8 kg/cycle of water. This water, with blum lumbs, could produce 17 kg of Algae, almost doubling the 18 kg/cycle of algae the terrarium already uses. Factoring the opportunity cost of this used water, the Algae Terrarium can only convert algae to oxygen at up to 75.4% mass efficiency.
Bog Bucket produces 150% as much algae per Blum Lumb than their other foods, but are only 78.4% as water efficient as Bristle Blossom, and only 36.2% as efficient as Ovagro Fig.
Oxygen conversion gets even more efficient with Fertilization, Pollination, and Mutation. While ovagro fig can be fertilized and pollinated, it's prohibitively inefficient, as each vine must be individually boosted. Ovagro figs can not have seed mutations.
A fertilized and Grubgrub or Mimika pollinated bristle blossom is more water efficient than ovagro figs. An Exuberant bristle blossom is likewise more water efficient than an ovagro fig.
Exuberant Bristle Blossoms, fertilized by a Bionic Duplicant with 8 Crop Tending Booster, and pollinated by a Grubgrub 100% of the time, require 12188 g/cycle Water, plus 263 g/cycle Polluted Water (and trace amounts of dirt and phosphorite), to feed each Blum Lumb, converting water to nearly 960% its mass in oxygen. At these rates, each plant supports 2.46 Blumb Lumbs.


== Water Cycling via Peat Burner ==
A Peat Burner requires 600 kg/cycle of Peat and produces 480W and 120 kg/cycle of Polluted Water. To run a Peat Burner at full capacity, the peat output of 3 Lumbs is required if fed Ovagro Fig or Bristle Berry, or 2 Lumbs if fed Bog Jelly.

When fed Ovagro Fig, each Lumb would require the production of 12 Ovagro Vine, or half of a fully developed Ovagro Node. One Ovagro Node can support 2 Lumbs, and consumes 90 kg/cycle of Water, or 45 kg/cycle per Lumb. A Peat Burner requires the output of 3 Lumbs for continuous operation, or 160W and 40 kg/cycle of Polluted Water per Lumb. Thus recycling the Polluted Water from the Peat Burner back into Water and feeding it back into the Ovagro Nodes is almost water-neutral, requiring the addition of only 5 kg/cycle of Water per Lumb (plus 8 kg/cycle per lumb of Filtration Medium, if a Water Sieve is used to cleanse the Polluted Water).
If Lumbs are fed with Bristle Berry, 4.875 Bristle Blossoms are required per Lumb, at a sum cost of 97.5 kg/cycle Water.  As the Peat Burner only returns 40 kg/cycle Polluted Water per Lumb, this is significantly more water-negative than feeding them with Ovagro Figs, costing a net of 57.5 kg/cycle per Lumb of additional water input (as well as more filtration medium if using Water Sieve).
Each Lumb requires 4.66 Bog Buckets, at a sum cost of 186.5 kg/cycle of Polluted Water per Lumb. Two Lumbs fed on Bog Jelly are needed per Peat Burner, raising the Polluted Water return from the Peat Burner to 60 kg/cycle per Lumb, which is still less than a third of the input. This is the worst case of all three choices in terms of water recycling, requiring a net of 126.5 kg/cycle per Lumb of additional water input, 25 times the water input per cycle when using Ovagro Figs.  However, the increase in Peat yield per Lumb provides it a noteworthy space savings (32 cells of ranch space per Peat Burner, versus 48 per with the other two feed options). In addition, Bog Buckets are irrigated with Polluted Water directly, skipping the need to clean the Polluted Water from the Peat Burner.
 With the Exuberant Plant Mutation, 1/4 as many Bog Buckets or Bristle Blossoms are required per Lumb.
5 Exuberant Bristle Blossoms can feed 4 Lumbs, costing 100 kg/cycle of Water to produce 800 kg/cycle of Peat, sufficient to feed 1.33 Peat Burners and gross 160 kg/cycle of Polluted Water, or 60 kg/cycle net.
7 Exuberant Bog Buckets can feed 6 Lumbs, costing 280 kg/cycle of Polluted Water to produce 1800 kg/cycle of Peat, sufficient to feed 3 Peat Burners and gross 360 kg/cycle of Polluted Water, or 80 kg/cycle net.
Regardless of food selected, it is recommended to ranch Lumbs in the same room as their food supply, allowing the Lumbs to harvest the plants rather than requiring additional duplicant labor.
Note that if pollinators or micronutrient fertilizers are used, the Ovagro Fig pathway can be made water positive.

Mealwood is a food plant that grows from a Mealwood Seed.


== Seed ==
The Mealwood Seed can be obtained by harvesting and uprooting Mealwood, or by digging up a Buried Object within the Sandstone Biome. It grows into Mealwood when planted.
Like any other seed, it can be fed to Pacus to domesticate them, and excrete Polluted Dirt.


== Food ==
One domesticated Mealwood plant produces 1 Meal Lice (600 kcal) every 3 cycles (if you do harvest errand immediately!) and consumes 10kg Dirt/cycle.

1 Meal Lice (600kcal)
1 Meal Lice (30kg Dirt) + 50kg Water can be processed in the Microbe Musher into 1 Liceloaf (1700 kcal)
3 Meal Lice can be processed in the Electric Grill into 1 Pickled Meal (1800 kcal)
600 kcal / 3 cycles = 200 kcal/cycle/plant. Thus, when eating raw meal lice, you need exactly1 a minimum of 5 domesticated Mealwood plants or 20 wild mealwood per Duplicant. Domesticated also consumes 50kg Dirt/cycle.
1 If your Duplicants don't do the harvest errand immediatelly, the Meal Lice remains on the plant for 1 cycle, then it drops on the ground (and begins to rot). And only after that, will the cycle to grow a new Meal Lice begin anew! Should you use Auto-Sweeper to do the "harvesting", you need to calculate with one full additional cycle: 600/4=150kcal/cycle/plant and then 6,666…7 plants per Duplicant!


=== Sustainability ===
Either employ Pips to plant wild Mealwood plants or find a sustainable source for Dirt:

one Pip produces 20 kg of Dirt/cycle and consumes 9% growth of Arbor Trees and 20% growth of Thimble Reeds per cycle.
…


=== General considerations ===
Consuming as Liceloaf has a bonus of (1,700/1,200) ≈ 1.4. 200 kcal * 1.4 = 280 kcal/cycle/plant. Dupes need around 1,000 kcal/cycle, so you need around four plants per dupe. While Pickled Meal does not provide an increase in Calories, the increased storage times will allow you to build up your food reserves before you're able to build a refrigerator. Making it also provides training in Cooking for your future dedicated Chef. 
The advantage of Meal Lice is that it is simple to grow. Together with Dusk Cap, it requires no irrigation of any kind. It also only requires dirt as its fertilizer, and doesn't require extreme temperatures. This makes it useful in the early game, when the Forest Biome's minimal water must be spent efficiently. However, it should be noted that despite the ease of obtaining Dirt, sustained farming of Mealwood requires a perpetual source of dirt, since composting rotten Meal Lice is unable to replenish it. While Quality foods also provide higher calories, the amount of calories in the Mealwood is still more than enough to supply even a fairly populous base, so the main reason to improve your farms away from Meal Lice is for the increased Morale bonus.


== Growth ==
Mealwood requires temperature range of 10 °C ↔ 30 °C / 50 °F ↔ 86 °F, and air pressure of 150 g - 10 kg. It requires Oxygen, Polluted Oxygen or Carbon Dioxide atmosphere.


=== Wild ===
A wild Mealwood takes 12 cycles to grow to maturity. 


=== Domestic ===
Mealwood can be planted in a Planter Box, a Farm Tile or a Hydroponic Farm. It needs to be fertilized with 10 kg/cycle of Dirt.
A domestic Mealwood takes 3 cycles to grow to maturity.
Mealwood can be planted from Mealwood Seeds acquired from digging wild Mealwood or uncovering buried objects.


== Notes ==
Meal Lice is less calorie dense than most other food items: a single kilogram of Meal Lice is only 600 kcal (for comparison, a 1kg Frost Bun is 1200 kcal). However, this is only really relevant for Storage capacity, and possibly producing Rot Piles.
A Mealwood Plant has a decor value of -10 with 2 tiles radius.

Megafrond is a cold dwelling plant found in the Feather Biome; it produces Megafrond Grain.


== Seed ==
Megafrond Spore can be obtained by uprooting a Megafrond in the Feather Biome. They can be obtained from Care Packages after Cycle 48. They cannot be obtained by harvesting Megafrond Grain, and unlike Sleet Wheat Grain for Sleet Wheat, Megafrond Grain is not the plant's seed.


== Growth ==
A Megafrond requires a temperature range of -45 °C ↔ 15 °C / -49 °F ↔ 59 °F, and an air pressure of 500 g ↔ 10000 g. It requires an atmosphere of Chlorine.
Megafrond's growth speed cannot be boosted by using Micronutrient Fertilizer on it. 


=== Wild ===
It requires 13.5 kg/cycle (22.5 g/s) Chlorine, which it draws directly from its environment.
A wild Megafrond takes 36 cycles to grow.


=== Domestic ===
It can be planted in a Planter Box, a Farm Tile or a Hydroponic Farm.
It requires 54 kg/cycle (90 g/s) Chlorine, which it draws directly from its environment.
A domestic Megafrond takes 9 cycles to grow.


== Food ==
Megafrond Grain can be used to make Frost Buns (and thus Frost Burgers), Pepper Bread, Soufflé Pancakes, Berry Sludge, Mixed Berry Pie, Fish Taco, and Shellfish Tempura.
In all recipes that require it, Megafrond Grain can be substituted by an equal amount of Sleet Wheat Grain.
In most recipes, each Megafrond Grain is worth 400 kcal when prepared. 
Megafrond drops 36 Megafrond Grains every 9 cycles. Although Megafrond Grains are not directly edible, if cooked into Frost Buns, each Megafrond produces 1,600 kcal/cycle, which is 4 times the yield per cycle of Sleet Wheat, and 1.33 times the yield per horizontal tile as Sleet Wheat.


=== Spoilage ===
Megafrond Grain will spoil in Oxygen or Polluted Oxygen, and in temperatures above -18 °C / -0.4 °F. Since a Megafrond grows in Chlorine, when it matures and drops its Megafrond Grain, it will benefit from the Sterile Atmosphere modifier, decreasing its decay rate. If the Chlorine is kept below -18 °C / -0.4 °F, the Megafrond Grain will also benefit from the Deep Freeze modifier, effectively preventing it from spoiling entirely.

Morbs are non-hostile, land-based critters that can be found naturally in the Caustic Biome. They passively excrete Polluted Oxygen and consume nothing. While they cannot be tamed, they can be captured with a Critter Trap and delivered to a Critter Drop-Off. 


== Spawning ==
If an Outhouse is filled, left unemptied, and not disabled, a Morb will spawn near it after 2 cycles. 
An Outhouse will only spawn a Morb ONCE after 2 cycles, but more can be spawned again by resetting the Outhouse state. This is done by reloading the game or simply by disabling/enabling the Outhouse (whether it's from the duplicant's toggling action or by having the Outhouse built on top of a Mechanized Airlock which cycles open/close). It makes refilling the Outhouse unnecessary to get more spawns.
Crashed Satellites have a chance to spawn three Morbs when rummaged.
Outhouses made unavailable due to gunk from Bionic Duplicants will not spawn Morbs.


== Behavior ==
Morbs are not hostile and will try to flee when attacked. They will wander in one direction until they cannot travel further, then turn and travel back. They have the ability to jump walls that are 2 tiles high or across a one tile gap. Like other critters, they may be trapped permanently inside of doors and Mesh Tiles.
Morbs, like Pufts, only achieve their maximum production rate if their mobility is limited and if never over-pressured. They will otherwise spend much of their time traveling or idling instead of producing.


== Mechanics ==
Periodically, they will emit a cloud with 200 g of Polluted Oxygen infected with 200 germs of Slimelung if their current tile meets certain conditions:
Not in Vacuum or occupied by Liquids.
Atmospheric pressure below 1,000 g.
Arrived at this tile on its last movement.
If the second tile above them is not blocked, Morbs will show an "emission" animation at this point. It is not required.
Morbs produce Slimelung germs.
Morbs' exact rates of production are difficult to specify precisely:
Morb emissions happen 0-3 times every time the Morb ends a Movement, and are therefore highly random and dependent on many specific circumstances.
A single Morb with 7 to 9 tiles of running space in a closed chamber of 100 g of polluted oxygen was tested to producing an average of 60 emissions, or 12 kg/cycle, at fast game speed.
The Morb rate of Polluted Oxygen emissions is slightly affected by in-game speed and lag, this is likely due to a reduced number of critter movement checks on lower frame rates. A slow game speed may make the Morbs generate 1 g/s to 2 g/s extra Polluted Oxygen.
At least 2 tiles of running space is needed for any production at all, Morbs will not produce in a 1 tile restricted space.
Morbs cannot be overcrowded or unhappy, so you can put a large number of them in a small room and it will not additionally impact their production rate.


== Tips ==
Since only one type of germ can exist in any kind of tile, putting Buddy Buds next to the Morbs will effectively prevent their Slimelung production, since the Polluted Oxygen will carry Floral Scents instead.
An Atmo Sensor should be paired with anything harvesting the emission clouds (Gas Pumps, Deodorizers, ...), to both protect the Morbs from Vacuum penalties, and allow the Buddy Buds to work (they must have at least 150 g of atmospheric pressure).
Morbs output Polluted Oxygen from nothing, and thus are resource-positive by themselves, enabling usage of Polluted Oxygen.
Pufts stables can be fed solely with Morbs to get Slime for free, and thus Algae (from Algae Distiller), Coal (from Sage Hatches) or even Dirt (from melting). Under optimal settings, 4.2 Morbs are needed for each Puft, and 2.5 for each Puft Prince. A full Puft ranch with 10 Pufts + 1 Prince Puft will need at least 45 Morbs to be sustained.
A Deodorizer room to mass-produce Clay and Oxygen can be set up above the Morbs. To properly separate the Polluted Oxygen and Oxygen atmospheres, the Deodorizers must be placed on Mesh Tiles, themselves placed on Airflow Tiles, with Water inside the Mesh Tiles. The Deodorizers have the range to reach gases inside the Airflow Tiles, and will output Oxygen at their level, above the liquid. Note that, because Deodorizers don't have a pressure limit, this can produce high atmospheric pressure, with all its drawbacks (e.g. causing the Popped Eardrums effect on duplicants). At least 5 Morbs are needed per Deodorizer to have 100% uptime.
An optimal Morb farming setup would be an infinitely long completely flat running path to allow maximum movement opportunities and the quickest completion of them, but any flat space 7 tiles wide and up would be practically identical in terms of efficiency.
Spawning a lot of Morbs will make their Polluted Oxygen production bottlenecked by the atmospheric pressure, effectively mitigating the seemingly randomness of their emission rate (due to RNG, in-game speed, and lag).
To keep spawning Morbs from the Outhouses without paying attention to the cycle count, you can reload the game every time a new Printable is available from the Printing Pod.
Gases heavier than Polluted Oxygen, such as Carbon Dioxide, will displace the emission clouds, allowing you to maintain a steady atmospheric pressure for your Morbs even in rooms above 1,000 g.
 Morbs provide an infinitely renewable source of oxygen for duplicant survival on planetoids lacking water or oxygen geysers.

Orehulls are large aquatic critters found in the Kelp Forest Biome. They feed on Kelpoles and Nori and excrete Polluted Mud. They can also be sheared for Iron Ore. 


== Behavior ==
 →  → 
Orehulls, like Jawbos are large 2x2 aquatic critters, although before adulting, their size is only 1x1. In wild they are usually found in Polluted Water in the Kelp Forest Biome, however, they survive just fine in other liquids as well. They can eat Kelpoles alive, as well as Nori that drops from them. When crowded, orehulls will cull kelpoles they can reach, without eating them, simply letting the Nori they drop fall on the ground.


== Diet ==
A tamed and groomed Orehull will eat 2 kelpoles or 20 kg of Nori per cycle and excrete 50 kg/cycle of Polluted Mud. Feeding them Nori and Kelpoles is essentially equivalent in terms of the amount of Tower Kelp needed per an Orehull. A single domesticated Tower Kelp ideally produces about 2.66 kelpoles per cycle, which is enough to feed 1.33 Orehulls. However, in practice, this number will be smaller, due to the time spent by duplicants harvesting kelpoles. Domestic Tower Kelp consumes Polluted Dirt and Polluted Water, both of which can be obtained by decomposing the Polluted Mud orehulls excrete on a Sludge Press. This is net positive in terms of polluted water, but slightly net negative in terms of polluted dirt.  


== Ranching ==
Orehull ranching and shearing is a renewable source of Iron Ore and a source of Raw Shellfish.They are also the only renewable source of Polluted Mud.
As Orehulls are aquatic critters, ranching them requires an Aquatic Grooming Station, while shearing them for iron ore will require an Aquatic Shearing Station. Aquatic Critter Condo and an Aquatic Critter Fountain can also be optionally added to increase their reproduction rate.
The main difficulty of ranching orehulls comes from their diet. Tower Kelp plants - the source of their food require quite a lot of space. Growing tower kelp inside their ranch is a viable option: while Kelpoles can cause crowding, orehulls will kill them them immediately, as long as they can access them. Nori that they drop takes a long time to spoil can also be eaten by Orehulls without any losses in efficiency in comparison to alive Kelpoles. 
It is therefore almost equally viable to grow Tower Kelp separately and feed Orehulls with Nori they drop. Spoilage is not an issue, since it takes Nori 32 cycles to spoil, so Orehulls should be able to eat most of it on time. The body of water in which kelpoles dwell in that case should be separate from that of any other critters to avoid crowding. 
Domestic Tower Kelp consumes Polluted Water, a sufficient amount of which can be obtained by decomposing Polluted Mud, excreted by the orehulls on a Sludge Press. Polluted Dirt is also required by the tower kelp and is also obtained this way, however, the amount of the polluted dirt is not sufficient to form a self-sufficient loop. An Orehull in tandem with domestic Tower Kelp generates about 6.6 kg of polluted water per cycle, while consuming about 10 kg of polluted dirt, which will need to be supplied from elsewhere. 
If wild tower kelp is used, 3 plants are required per an orehull. This is not very space efficient, since 3 fully grown tower kelp plants alone take 30 tiles.
