Ovagro Node is a plant that produces Ovagro Vines. If unimpeded, the node can grow up to 12 vines on each side. These vines grow Ovagro Figs as food.


== Seed ==
The Ovagro Node Seed is the seed of Ovagro Node. It can be obtained by uprooting an Ovagro Node, digging buried objects in the Garden Biome, and harvesting Ovagro Figs from Ovagro Vines.
The seeds are also obtainable through the Printerceptor story trait.

Harvesting Ovagro Figs from a Ovagro Vine produces seeds at 16× the rate of a normal plant. For example, if a Duplicant ordinarily has a 60% seed chance when harvesting a plant, then harvesting an Ovagro Vine would only have a 10% chance of producing a seed
 Harvesting Ovagro Vines do not produce mutated seeds


== Usage ==
Lumbs consumes 1,300 kcal/cycle of Ovagro Fig, a food that drops from an Ovagro Vine.


== Growth ==
Upon planting, an Ovagro Node is immediately mature but produces no fruit. Instead, it spawns two Ovagro Vines - one on each side. Each vine requires 3 cycles to reach maturity (12 cycles if wild). Once mature, a vine bears Ovagro Fig every 3 cycles (12 cycles if wild) and continues to generate additional adjacent vines until there are 12 vines on each side or there is no more room to expand.
Ovagro Vines can only expand into cells that are:

Unoccupied by other plants, non-background buildings or any Liquid.
Supported by a foundation - either a tile or any door (including Pneumatic Doors).
Once these requirements are met, a vine can grow even alongside walls or on a ceiling.
The Farmer's touch effect is applied to individual vines costing significantly more fertilizer than other plants, however this can also accelerate the growth of further vines


== Food ==
Each Ovagro Vine bears fruit every 3 cycles, which can be harvested for 325 kcal of Ovagro Fig. This gives the Ovagro Node a variable range of food production, ranging from 108 to 2600 kcal/cycle depending on the number of vines that have matured (between 1 and 24 vines, respectively). As the water consumption is fixed, this makes the Ovagro Node the most water-efficient plant for food ( but behind the Exuberant mutations of plants like Bristle Blossom and Sleet Wheat).
Ovagro Fig can be further cooked into Mixed Berry Pie.


== Tips ==
The Park and Nature Reserve rooms do not count vines as wild plants for room requirement purposes. Only the node counts as a single wild plant.

The Oxyfern is a non-reproducing plant that converts Carbon Dioxide  into breathable Oxygen . The rate is related to the air pressure, and a lower air pressure will result in less Oxygen production.


== Seed ==
Oxyfern Seeds can be obtained by uprooting Oxyferns, by digging up a Buried Object within the Forest Biome, or as a Care Package. It grows into a Oxyfern when planted.


== Ratios ==
The Oxyfern has a quite similar gas conversion rates to Duplicants, however they are about 3.2 times slower, and produce slightly more Oxygen  than Duplicants consume, which makes it impossible to cleanly match their number to the number of Duplicants, leading to either Oxygen or Carbon Dioxide  runaway overproduction.

Domesticated Oxyferns convert about 98% of Water   to Oxygen , which is about 10% more water-efficient than the Electrolyzer (88% Water to Oxygen), with the additional cost of 4kg per cycle Dirt .
As with any other plant, wild Oxyferns produce four times slower compared to domesticated ones, however they do not require Water or Dirt.


== Growth ==
Oxyferns requires temperature range of 0 °C ↔ 40 °C / 32 °F ↔ 104 °F. It requires air pressure of 25g to 10kg, and a Carbon Dioxide  atmosphere. The plant has no growth cycle.
Domestic Oxyferns can be planted in a Planter Box, Farm Tile and Hydroponic Farm. It requires 4kg per cycle Dirt  and irrigation of 19kg per cycle Water  .


== Heat economy ==
Since they produce 50 grams of Oxygen  at their body temperature for every gram of Carbon Dioxide  consumed, and Oxygen has 20% more specific heat than Carbon Dioxide, they have some heat deletion potential if the plants can be kept cool enough to grow in an atmosphere of very hot Carbon Dioxide. This is made easier by Carbon Dioxide's poor heat potential.
A single domestic Oxyfern kept at 1 °C / 33.8 °F and slowly fed 500 °C / 932 °F Carbon Dioxide, similar to that from a carbon dioxide vent, will delete 0.625g/s and 100 DTU/s in Carbon Dioxide  relative to a target base temperature of 20 °C / 68 °F, and produce 31.3g/s cold Oxygen  with a cooling potential of 600 DTU/s, for a total heat deletion of approximately 700 DTU/s, about half that of a wild Wheezewort growing in Oxygen, or a twentieth of a domestic Wheezewort grown in Hydrogen.
In general, the Oxyfern heats and cools very slowly while growing because they convert a small amount of the atmosphere they're inside to a much larger amount of atmosphere at their own body temperature, cooling the area if it's warmer than them and warming it if it's cooler.
A single non-geotuned Carbon Dioxide Vent produces about 105 g/s on average of Carbon Dioxide  at 500 °C / 932 °F, enough to feed 170 domestic Oxyferns, which can completely delete the Carbon Dioxide and replace it with 5.2kg/s of Oxygen, providing oxygen for 26 Duplicants and providing 100 kDTU/s of heat deletion relative to a 20 °C / 68 °F base if the Oxyferns are kept at 1 °C / 33.8 °F. Obtaining this many Oxyfern Seeds is impractical however, since they only spawn on map creation or are offered as a rare care package.


== Pressure management ==
Oxyferns have a very high upper pressure limit for growth, and multiply the pressure of their input gas by 50, producing 50 grams of Oxygen  for every gram of Carbon Dioxide  consumed. 
Left unsealed, unchecked Oxygen or Carbon Dioxide production might eventually overpressure your base. Since they will operate at a higher pressure range than a Electrolyzer, Oxygen Diffuser, and standard gas vents, Oxygen production from these will automatically stop if the Oxyferns raise Oxygen pressure in their areas too high. With good gas diffusion in your base and Oxyfern farms, this means that overpressure from Oxyferns alone will not happen as long as your Oxyferns alone produce less Oxygen  than you're consuming. This does however have the unfortunate side effect of shutting down hydrogen gas production from any Electrolyzers which will slow down or stop due to increased ambient Oxygen, which can impact power generation.
If kept in a sealed box, it is extra important to remember that Oxyferns multiply the mass of gas inputs by 50, so Oxyferns initially grown at the bottom of a sealed box of 2kg per tile Carbon Dioxide  will eventually convert the room into 80% Oxygen and 20% Carbon Dioxide at 10kg per tile, at which point the Oxyferns will stop growing due to overpressure. The highest Carbon Dioxide pressure at which they will never overpressure in a sealed room is 200g Carbon Dioxide per tile, which they will convert to 10kg per tile Oxygen. This setup has the advantage of not requiring the player to worry about Oxyferns overpressurizing the base but requires pumping Carbon Dioxide in and Oxygen out.


== Tips ==
Oxyfern Seeds are sometimes offered as a Care Package.
The only other way to increase the amount of Oxyferns on the map is via the Printerceptor story trait, besides seed-splitting exploits.

Pacu is an aquatic Critter found in pools in the Swamp Biome. They produce Fish Fillets and Eggs, and their morphs can provide either fresh Water or decor bonuses. They can be domesticated.


== Behavior ==
Pacu float around in liquids at the flooding level (over 35% of default mass), and will generally otherwise be in the "flopping" state; while flopping doesn't hurt them, it gives them confined status.
They have a short lifespan of 25 cycles and a high egg mass (4 kg). This makes them very useful for food and Lime. On death, they drop 1,000 kcal of Fish Fillet, which can be cooked into 1,600 kcal of Cooked Seafood at an Electric Grill.
Their excrement can be fed to Pokeshells for additional lime, although it takes about 22 to feed each.
Unlike most critters, which need to be groomed, Pacus are tamed by feeding from a Fish Feeder, and this takes much longer, about 6.66 cycles instead of the usual 2.
A Pacu is crowded if the sum of all aquatic creatures personal space requirement in the pool exceeds the size of the pool. The critter's happiness decreases by this difference, divided by that critter's personal space requirement (rounded up).
A Pacu is cramped if the sum of all aquatic creatures and eggs personal space requirement in the pool exceeds the size of the pool, with a minimum of 1 egg.
The pool size is the number of connected, non-navigable liquid cells. A non-navigable liquid cell is either a liquid cell that exceeds 35% of its default mass, or a liquid cell with another solid/liquid cell on top. Non-navigable cells can drown non-aquatic critters. Liquid inside Mesh Tiles and Pneumatic Doors also count and are treated as one pool of liquid with the surrounding liquid.
Aquatic critters in the same room but not in the pool will not impact a Pacus Crowdedness, although the Pacus will impact the Crowdedness of the normal critters.
Unlike other critters, they will not be confined when inside an open door.

Pacus will only swim into tiles of at least 35% default mass, and have trouble swimming into liquids that are not substantial. This can be used to limit Pacu movement for performance reasons or to help them reach their feed. Pacus that are not in tile of substantial liquid begin flopping. Flopping Pacus will look for the nearest body of liquid and attempt to move in that direction. While Flopping, Pacus will fall through Pneumatic Doors and open Manual Airlocks/Mechanized Airlocks.
All Pacus have a mass of 200 kg when hatched and when they reach adulthood. Newly born Pacu have body temperatures which are specific to their variant, resulting in heat creation/deletion.

A large pool filled with these critters can produce enough fresh water to support a base though water needs to be siphoned off quickly thanks to its higher freezing point than Polluted Water. Alternatively, if the Polluted Water is cold enough the water that the Gulp Fish produces will instantly freeze into Ice, which can be collected and melted.
The water that Gulp Fish produce matches their internal body temperature, which can cause massive heat creation/deletion depending on a Gulp Fish's temperature relative to the Polluted Water that it takes in.
When Gulp Fish hatch and reach adulthood, their temperature is -12.5 °C / 9.5 °F.


== Pacu Ranching ==


=== Tamed Pacu ===
A newly-born tame Pacu will live long enough to lay an egg, even when not fed, as long as it is not kept with too many other Pacu (9 in 8 tiles of liquid will work). This allows some limited starvation ranching potential, but the yield is rather low considering the investment in materials to set up systems to automatically store the starving Pacu and remove eggs.
Alternatively, simply cooking a tame, fed Pacu's 13 spare eggs over its 25 cycle lifespan into Omelette, at 5600 kcal each due to their large size, provides 2912 kcal per cycle average.
It is possible to sustain a single Pacu-breeder via Algae Distiller-Pufts pathway. One Pacu requires 7.5 kg of Algae per cycle. The 7.5 kg of Algae require 22.5 kg of slime per cycle, which can be covered with some excess by 1 tame Puft. This in turn would need 50 kg of Polluted Oxygen per cycle. Off-gassing such an amount from polluted water would require around 1700 kg of Polluted Water at the surface, or around 2100 kg of bottled Polluted Water for offgassing. It can be supplemented by Polluted Oxygen Vents, Morbs and  Sublimation Stations, although Morbs' production rates are inconsistent.
As the Fish Feeder's Ate From Feeder effect does not depend on the amount of food consumed, it is possible to use very small amounts of food to keep a Pacu happy. This strategy saw more use when its Algae diet was extremely gluttonous.
An alternative option to Algae is to use seeds in your Fish Feeder, as these can be easily gained from a dedicated farm or just from the passive seed gain in your colony's other farms. When making a dedicated farm for the Pacu. The Balm Lily can work well due to the lack of a fertilizer requirement and so only needs dupe labor to harvest. Sleet Wheat and Nosh Sprouts are effective alternatives due to their yields being large numbers of seeds. Spigot Seals can be an excellent source of Bonbon Tree seeds. Finally, Mealwood, Sweatcorn, Pikeapple and Thimble Reeds all grow quickly, and can be effective at producing seeds when paired with a skilled Duplicant. Note that Arbor Acorns/Seakomb Seed cannot be fed to Pacu.
 Each Pacu can be sustained with 2 Seakomb plants. Note that the Polluted Dirt expelled by Pacus is also used as fertilizer for Seakomb but only at 50% efficiency. Alternatively, when Seakomb Leaf is processed into Phyto Oil using Plant Pulverizer, and heated to Algae, one Seakomb plant can sustain 3.5 Pacus, and the Polluted Dirt produced is enough to fully fertilize the Seakomb plant, but this needs a source of Water as it is consumed in the Plant Pulverizer recipe.


=== Wild Pacu ===
A newly-born wild Pacu will live long enough to lay an egg as long as it is not kept with too many other Pacu (up to 10 in 8 tiles of liquid will work). This allows some limited starvation ranching potential, but the yield is rather low considering the investment in materials to set up systems to automatically store the starving Pacu and remove eggs.
Note that wild Pacu can still become Cramped if they are overcrowded when one lays an egg. This can be avoided by moving the egg into another room.

Eggs retain the wildness of the parent at the time the egg is laid.

Pinpoket is a backwall plant, found in the Abyss Biome. It can be farmed for Pinpoki, which can be reprocessed into food or renewable Diamond 


== Seed ==
Pinpoket Seed can be obtained by harvesting and uprooting Pinpoket within the Abyss Biome. It grows into Pinpoket when planted.


== Growth ==
Pinpokets, like Starnacles are aquatic wall plants, which means that they can only be planted into Wall Planters for domestic growth, or into natural backwall tiles by Pips. Their temperature range requires them to be grown in warm enviroments, which their native biome already provides. They also require an atmosphere of Squid Ink any non-pure water type, which includes Polluted Brine that is readily available at a suitable temperature in Abyss Biome. It should be noted, however, that Polluted Brine Vents that can be found in the same biome generate Polluted Brine at the temperature of 95 °C / 203 °F, which is unsuitable for growing Pinpokets, meaning that such vents should eventually thermally isolated.
Pinpokets have a rather slow growth rate while also being a bulky 2x2 plant, so for most purposes a quite large amount of them is needed. 


=== Domestic ===
Pinpoket Seeds can be planted into Wall Planters by duplicants or Auto-Sweepers. In order for the plant to grow, all 4 of its cells must be submerged into a suitable fluid. Domestic Pinpokets must be fertilized with 5 kg/cycle of Refined Carbon . An Auto-Sweeper's range conveniently can fully fit up to 16 Wall Planers to supply them automatically. However, one can take advantage of the fact that the Tile of interest of a Wall Planter is the bottom left one, which allows to add extra plants, the amount of which would depend on the layout. 
If duplicants are used for harvesting Pinpoki, which is up to 25% more efficient than self-harvesting, they will have to be submerged and most likely - swim, using the respective skill. Swimming is slower in Atmo Suits, but they are needed, unless the temperature of the farm is kept closer to the lower end of Pinpoket's temperature range.


=== Wild ===
While Pip are able to plant wild Pinpoket Seeds, they require naturally generated backwall tiles for this, which cannot be created artificially. In adition to that, wild Pinpokets are very space inefficient: sustaining a single Marine Drill with Diamond  obtained from crashing Pinpoki would alone require 30 wild Pinpoket plants, occupying 120 tiles, not accounting for the spacing between them, needed for wild planting. 


== Usage ==
Pinpoki, harvested from these plants have 2 different uses: crushing them into Diamond  and cooking them into Uni.


=== Diamond production ===
Each Pinpoki unit can be crushed into 100 kg of Diamond by a duplicant using a Rock Crusher. Since growing a single Pinpoki domestically requires 96 Kg of Refined Carbon , this is essentially a slightly more resource-efficient alternative to a Diamond Press which doesn't require any Radbolts to function. However, a single domestic Pinpoket generates only 6.3 kg/cycle of Diamond , not accounting for harvest time. For supplying a Marine Drill with diamond, a bit less than 8 domestic Pinpokets are required, however for more ressource intensive purposes, such as supplying multiple Drillcones for space mining, using Diamond Presses even with all the infrastructure needed to create enough radbolts can become more efficient both in terms of space taken and in terms of labor.


=== Food ===
Alternatively, Pinpoki can be cooked on a Sushi Bar into 7200 kcal worth of Uni - a food item of Good (+3) quality. A single domestic Pinpoket, if used for food, generates up to 450 kcal of food per cycle, thus needing a bit over 2 plants per a duplicant. In addition to that, while Uni does spoil quickly like most foods, Pinpoki does not, meaning it can be stockpiled without needing any special conditions to be cooked only when needed. 
Interestingly, Uni has the highest Food Density in the game, making it technically the best food for feeding Experiment 52B. Doing so, however, would require at least 218 domestic Pinpokets or 872 tiles for the plants alone, making this quite space-inefficient.

== Behavior ==
They are able to cling strongly to any surface, and will freely wander the full perimeter of whatever chamber they are in. They are not hostile and are quite mobile, inevitably wandering away from any chamber they are not trapped in. They also seed hanging plants from the underside.
Occasionally, Pips navigate to storage containers and knock a debris type out of it, when piles amount for more than 1kg / 1 whole seed.

Another annoyance can be provided if they wander into empty farm plots, since they will plant seeds there too.

== Critter Morphs ==
Pips comes in two critter morphs. The chance of laying a Cuddle Pip egg is improved by eating Thimble Reeds. Even without eating Thimble Reeds, ordinary Pips come with an initial 2% chance of producing a Cuddle Pip egg.

The Cuddle Pip shares the same pip-planting behavior as the Pip, but can additionally cuddle eggs and hug duplicants. Cuddle Pips have the same diet as ordinary pips but consume 25% more and only requiring 4 tiles of personal space, allowing 3 times more cuddle pips to be ranched compared to pips.


==== Cuddling and Hugging ====
Twice a cycle, cuddle pips will search for an egg they can reach to try and cuddle it. Successful cuddles increase the incubation rate of the egg by 100%, which stacks with the incubator's lullabied buff. This buff cannot be stacked with itself, so the ideal scenario is to have twice as many eggs as cuddle pips in the room.
Twice per cycle (unless already successfully hugged), cuddle pips will stand up and look for hugs from passing duplicants for 30 seconds. If a duplicant hugs a cuddle pip, the pip will then try to cuddle every egg in the room for the next cycle. The hug will also provide the duplicant with a buff which provides -5% stress per cycle for half a cycle.
Note: Duplicants will not seek out pips to hug them. They will only hug a pip if they happen to pass by during the 30 second hug window.


== Building farms ==

It is possible to use their ability to plant plants in natural tiles to build farms that require no resources. It is possible to make a farm of plants planted on every other block horizontally and every 5 blocks vertically by forcing the Pips to plant from the top right going left and doing the rows from the top down. Hanging plants should instead be started from the bottom right, then left and moving up.
Pips will not plant a seed where the building is planned for construction. You can use this to your advantage by placing ceiling trims everywhere - this is extremely useful for ensuring pips plant seeds at the correct location to build farms that are optimally dense. Ceiling trims is arguably preferable over e.g. ladders as duplicants won't finish construction that are invalid placements, allowing you to easily cancel a construction task without needing to deconstruct.
There is a bug where two plants can be planted in the same spot, which prevents Pips from planting where it looks like they should.


=== 1-Space or 3-Space ===
Plants can either be planted in groups of 3, with 3 tiles between groups, or just 1 space between each plant. Creating a table to sum up the total amount of plants in a horizontal space of a given amount of tiles will show two scenarios. In the first, using 3 spaces between groups of 3 plants will be more space efficient, and in the second scenario, the two methods will be equal in efficiency.

This pattern repeats for every 6 tiles, which then makes the most efficient use of space for pip-planting being 6n+3. (3, 9, 15 ... )


=== Creating natural tiles ===
(see Natural Tile)


=== Dense Arbor Tree Farm ===
Pips' nimble paws allow them to plant seeds in Farm Tiles between Arbor Trees that Duplicants can't. A space efficient farm can be built by dispensing seeds and a pip in an enclosed room with farm tile floor. Eventually, all tiles will be planted by the pip. The same trick applies to a Farm Tile adjacent to other buildings as well, as long as the 3 tiles space above it is not obstructed.


== Regular Pip Ranching ==
(The following only applies to regular pips)
Pips require 0.32 wild or 0.08 domestic Arbor Trees per Pip to stay fed. A maximum size ranch (8 pips) can be supported by 2.56 wild or 0.64 domestic Arbor Tree (after the tree is mature and growing branches).
Pip eggs can be cracked to produce 1kg of Raw Egg which can be cooked into 2800kcal of Omelette. Alternatively the egg can be hatched and the pip killed to produce 1kg of Meat which can be cooked into 2000kcal of Barbeque. 
If never crowded and always groomed, a pip will produce 15 eggs during its 100 cycle lifespan. Cooking the eggs (leaving one to replace the pip) and final meat would yield a total of 41200kcal or 412kcal/cycle over the pip's lifetime. This puts a lower limit of ~2.427 pips to feed one duplicant on default difficulty. 
Pips can process wild Arbor Trees into free dirt. One Pip can supply 2 Mealwood plants or domestic Arbor Trees, 4 Nosh Sprouts or Sleet Wheat plants, or 5 Oxyferns. A shared ranch with seven Pips and a single Sage Hatch can act as a low-maintenance source of Coal. Two Pips can keep a Fertilizer Synthesizer running constantly (with some dirt left over). A single Pip ranch can supply 16 Mealwood, which will feed 16 Glossy Dreckos, or exactly enough for two full Drecko ranches.
Pips can rummage through Arbor Tree branches for Arbor Acorns - this is the only way to acquire additional acorns. They can reach all branches from the base of the arbor tree.


== Cuddle Pip Ranching ==
Converting ranches from regular pips to cuddle pips may be an effective means to increase both dirt and food production. It is important to note that this relies on the ability to fit additional cuddle pips in each ranch compared to regular pips. Each cuddle pip produces the same egg and meat output as a regular pip, but only produces 5/8 (.625) the amount of dirt. The logical conclusion is that any ranch that can support additional pips can convert to cuddle to increase the food output, but cuddle ranches need at least 12.8 satisfied cuddle pips to match the dirt output of 8 regular pips. 
Cuddle pips require 0.4 wild or 0.1 domestic Arbor Tree per Cuddle Pip to stay fed (assuming 5 branches per tree). A maximum size ranch can be supported by 9.6 wild or 2.4 domestic Arbor Trees.

Thimble Reeds can also be used to feed pips, and is almost required to get pips to lay cuddle pip eggs. Each cuddle pip requires 2 wild thimble reeds, or 0.5 domestic thimble reeds, making it much costlier and/or space-inefficient than using Arbor Trees. However, using wild Exuberant thimble reeds has a slightly smaller footprint than using wild arbor trees.


== Bonbon Tree versus Arbor Tree Comparison ==
Feeding through Bonbon Trees are very similar to arbor trees. They have the same ratios as arbor trees (0.32 wild arbor trees, or 0.08 domestic arbor trees per Pip. 0.4 wild domestic tree, or 0.01 domestic trees per Cuddle Pip) but poses a few key differences:

Slightly larger footprint, as 2 cells of space are needed between trees.
Inflexible branch pattern compared to arbor trees.
Incompatible environments. Bonbon trees prefer chilly temperatures between -75 °C ↔ -15 °C / -103 °F ↔ 5 °F, which is much lower than what pips are comfortable in.
Each branch needs to be in contact with a source of light to grow, although it does not need to be the full 10,000 Lux (Bright).
Bonbon tree branches need to be fully grown before pips can eat it, significantly lengthening the time it takes to start up a pip farm. This also makes bonbon trees marginally less productive, as fully grown branches do not continue growing while waiting to be eaten.
Bonbon trees may grow in a vacuum, which arbor trees cannot.
Indeed, given the opportunity one should almost always prefer to use arbor trees. Bonbon tree would only really be preferable if you must ranch in a vacuum or arbor acorns are not available.

Plug Slug is a Critter found in the Swampy Biome (Spaced Out). They produce Hydrogen, Eggs, Meat, and generate Power. They can be domesticated. The Morphs act as biological pumps for non breathable gasses and liquids.


== Behavior ==
Similar to Dreckos and Pips, Plug Slugs are able to scale walls and walk along the ceiling. During the night Plug Slugs will nest on a ceiling and hang down, creating a socket two tiles below the ceiling (the lower tile of the slug) from which power can be drained. They will prefer to plug themselves onto exposed wires. Two Slugs cannot sleep on the same tile, and their socket cannot overlap buildings such as Storage Bins. 
They emit up to 400 Watts if wild, or up to 1600 Watts when tamed. The output for slugs will be lower if they are hungry, down to 40 W when starving.
Since Nighttime lasts 75 seconds on a 600s cycle, this means they generate on average up to 50W when wild or 200W when tame (up to 3 basic batteries or 3/4 of Jumbo Battery per wild slug per night). For reference, this puts a fully fed domesticated Plug Slug (or four wild) on par with a Manual Generator. 
Plug Slugs can eat all kinds of unrefined Metal Ores and Refined Metal, and excrete Hydrogen when they do so.  
Cracking a Plug Slug Egg yields 1000g of Raw Egg and 100g of Egg Shell.
It drops 3200 kcal (2 kg) of Meat on death.


== Location ==
A number of Plug Slugs can be found on the Swampy Asteroid in the Spaced Out DLC. This number varies, but at minimum is 5 fully mature Slugs. Since they can only output at night (a 75-second window), and do so at up to 10 kg/s, the maximum that can be transferred into pipes per cycle is 750 kg/cycle.
Similar to critter replacement of Liquid Pump.


== Ranching ==


=== vs Hatches for Power ===
Well-fed Hatches produce 70kg Coal per cycle. A Coal Generator uses 1kg Coal per second to produce 600W. Effectively generating 0.6*70 = 42 kJ of energy per critter per day.
Well-fed Plug Slugs produce 1600 W of power per Night (75 Seconds) or 1.6*75 = 120 kJ of direct energy per critter per day.
Well-fed Plug Slugs also produce 3kg of Hydrogen per day, which can power an 800W Hydrogen Generator for 30 seconds for an additional 24 kJ of storable energy per critter per day.
This combines to a total of 144 kJ per critter per day.
If the Plug Slugs are tame but glum, then food requirement and hydrogen output is reduced by 80%, but the direct power production remains the same. Per unit of food tame-glum Plug Slugs are 5x more effecient at producing power than tame-happy Plug Slugs, and 4x more efficient than Wild Plug Slugs.


=== Semi-starvation exploit ===
Starving Plug Slugs can be fed just before night to generate 800 W instead of 40 W at night, while starving for the rest of the day. This is much more efficient per-food than feeding the Slug all day. To take this exploit even further, Plug Slugs decide how much power they will generate at the moment they become drowsy and it doesn't matter if they subsequently cross a threshold that should cause them to produce less power, this means they only need to be non-starving for a few seconds when they become non-drowsy and so only a little food need to be given right before they become drowsy (allocating enough time for the Slug to react to the food and eat it). Approximate food requirements:

It can be seen that dramatic improvements in energy to food ratio can be achieved by exploiting the particular mechanics of power generation, with the most exploitative strategies producing at least 60x more energy per food than grooming and feeding the Plug Slugs.


== Uses ==
Plug Slugs consume metals and metal ores, both of which are valuable resources that are needed in large quantities. Considering the resource consumption, Plug Slugs are hard to maintain, and are thus a suboptimal source or power. However, they do still have some niched uses, especially when taken wild ranching into account.
The other morphs of the Slugs' family, however, are not as useful as their mechanical counterparts, in addition to being hard to set-up. A better choice would be to use the power-producing morph, and pair with batteries and pumps.


=== Remote Colony ===
Wild Plug Slugs produce power for free, enabling easy access to power wherever they are brought to. 
They are much easier to set up compared to some other forms of input-free power sources, such as wild arbor ethanol power. This characteristic makes Slug power useful if you don't want to spend too much time on a planetoid, or don't want to bring dupes with Mechatronics Engineering skill  In addition, it does not require access to the surface, making it a valid alternative to solar. This characteristic is useful when colonising the Regolith Asteroid.


=== Super Sustainable ===
The use of Plug Slugs does not disable the Super Sustainable Achievement, and the electricity they produce do count towards the progress.


=== Non-Oxygen Gas Filter ===
Smog Slugs only breath in gases that aren't breathable, making it useful to filter out carbon dioxide and other miscellaneous gases without relying on a Carbon Skimmer or filter.

=== Breeding Morphs ===
The volume of liquid required to change a Pokeshell's reproduction chance is 350 kg. The is the same level at which buildings flood. To operate, the Grooming Station must be placed out of the liquid, meaning the Pokeshells spend some of their time not in liquid. Starting from the correct base morph and assuming uninterrupted submersion, the cycle count needed for the probability of laying a critter morph roe egg is approximately:

95% correct egg chance: ~ 12.85 cycles
99% correct-egg chance: ~ 23.57 cycles
99.9% correct egg chance: ~ 38.93 cycles

Rhexes are carnivorous critters that feed on smaller Critters and produce Brine Ice. Their tailfeather can be shorn for Feather Fiber.


== Diet ==
Rhexes can either consume Meat or Tough Meat directly, or hunt live prey in the same room. Hunting live prey provides the same caloric intake as feeding the equivalent raw meat, but produces double the amount of Brine Ice as excretion.


==== Eligible Prey ====


== Life stages ==
 → → 


== Hunting ==
Hunting Live Prey is not a guaranteed act. To begin a hunt, both the Rhex and the prey must be in the same Room. Prey sitting inside doors will never be targeted by Rhexes.
A hunt is considered Wild if both its prey and the Rhex are wild. Otherwise, a hunt is considered Tame.
For Wild hunts:

The minimum percentage age of the prey, defined as Current AgeMax Age, is at least 82.5%.
Once this threshold is exceeded, the chance of a wild hunt succeeding is the prey’s percentage age plus 10% (max 100%).
For Tame hunts:

There is no minimum age requirement.
The chance of a tame hunt succeeding is the prey’s percentage age, scaled across the range 40% to 105%. For example, if the prey's percentage age is 50%, then the chance of a hunt succeeding will be at the 50 percentile between 40% to 105%, or 72.5%. This can be computed with the formula: Percentage Age⋅(1.05−0.4)+0.4
If a hunt fails, then the Rhex will not attempt another hunt for another 45 seconds.
Like most critters, Rhexes begin Looking For Food at 90% of their stomach size (calorie deficit of 800 kcal). A consequence of this is that almost all land critters (except for Dartle) drop more than 800 kcal of meat—when a Rhex feeds on live prey that would otherwise over‐satisfy its stomach, the remaining amount is dropped as Meat/Tough Meat. If that spillover meat is later consumed, no calories are lost, but the opportunity to produce Brine Ice is forfeited. Dartles are the only critter guaranteed not to overeat.
It also follows that feeding on live Shove Vole, Lumblet, and Bammini will always over‐satisfy the Rhex’s stomach.


== Synergy with Dartles ==
Rhex excretes Brine Ice to fertilize  Dew Drippers; the harvested Dewdrip then feeds Dartles, which Rhex can consume to complete the resource loop:
With 128 kg/cycle of Brine Ice from Live Prey, 12.8 Dew Drippers can feed 6.4 Dartle which produces about 1,433.6 kcal/cycle.
With 64 kg/cycle of Brine Ice from Meat, 6.4 Dew Drippers can feed 3.2 Dartle which produces about 716.8 kcal/cycle. This is only slightly less than the needed 800 kcal/cycle needed by a Rhex, and in practice require less Dew Dripper Plants when the Dartles' initial stomach calories are taken into account.
The Dartle is uniquely snack-sized to avoid Rhexes overeating behavior. This allows a simple means of guaranteeing the Rhexes' Brine Ice bonus from consuming Live Prey.


== Food economy ==
Rhex do not directly drop edible food. However, its Tough Meat can be cooked at a Smoker to produce 13,333 kcal of food. Happy Rhexes have a reproduction rate of 1 egg every 12 cycles and can reasonably lay 15 eggs in its lifetime. As a Rhex drops 5 kg of Tough Meat on death, it produces about 375 g of Tough Meat every cycle, which can be turned into 1,000 kcal of Tender Brisket every cycle.
If a Rhex is glum for less than 3 cycles in its lifetime, it is able to produce 16 eggs. This translates to 400 g of Tough Meat every cycle, which can be turned into 1,066 kcal of Tender Brisket every cycle.
If fed Meat, each Rhex consumes 800 kcal of Meat, equating to 1,000 kcal of Barbeque. This means that Rhex is better as a Brine Ice and Feather Fiber producer, instead of a food producer.


== Heat economy ==
Rhex will produce Brine Ice at its current body temperature. When hatching from an egg a Rhex will start at -17.5 °C / 0.5 °F. Heating 64 kilograms of Brine Ice from -17.5C to 25C takes 9,248,000 dtu. Assuming the Brine is then fed to a desalinator, this cooling method moves 1505.2 dtu/W while producing water and salt at 25C. Feeding the water to an electrolyzer and burning the Hydrogen Gas in an hydrogen Generator makes this process power positive.

An ice Maker can delete ~64.24 kDTU/s, so in this scenario one Rhex provides cooling equivalent to about 1/4 of an Ice Maker.
If the resulting Oxygen is fed to 3 dense Pufts, this loop is now oxylite and meat positive.
Rhex can be comfortable in -50C temperature. If Rhex is -40C, base temperature is 30C, and Rhex is fed live prey to double output, it would take 30,464,000 to heat the Brine to base temperature. This is equivalent to 4/5 of an Ice Maker.


== Cannibalistic Starvation Ranching ==
When a Rhex eats the Tough Meat dropped by a dead Rhex, it gains 10 cycles of Just Ate, the scale growth allows shearing up to 10 feathers, and during this time, if happy, it gains 88% egg progress, which combined with egg progress from its starting calories is easily enough to ensure one egg will be laid per lifetime. Starvation ranching of Rhexes mostly just produces feather, egg shell and brine ice. With careful allocation of the tough meat, not just allowing one starving Rhex to eat it all, it is possible to produce more than one egg per lifetime, actually increasing the population over time.

Pokeshell is a critter that lives in the Ocean Biome. They can live in both air and liquid and can be domesticated. They will consume both Rot Piles and Polluted Dirt at 70 kg/cycle, with Oakshells and Sanishells also consuming Slime.


== Behavior ==
Pokeshells drop 10 kg of Molt when they die (5 kg when a baby dies), which can be turned into Lime or Wood with the Rock Crusher. Normally, they are as non-hostile as other critters. However, once they can path to a Pokeshell egg fewer than 32 cells away, they become red and aggressive. When this happens, they will attack any Duplicant or critter in their way (shown as "protecting" in status tab), and beat them to death without exceptions if left unattended. They calm down and return to pink and innocent eyes again once they separated away from their eggs.


== Critter Morphs ==
Pokeshells have 3 critter morphs. Each Pokeshell has a different drop upon growth and death, but all consume Polluted Dirt  and produce Sand . Dwelling in Water   increases the chance of laying a Sanishell Roe, while dwelling in Ethanol   increases the chance of laying an Oakshell Roe. Not dwelling in either decreases those chances.


=== Pokeshell ===
 →  → 
Pokeshell consumes Polluted Dirt or Rot Pile and excretes Sand, and sheds shells that can be processed into Lime. A Pokeshell sheds a Pokeshell Molt when transitioning to an adult. On death, a Pokeshell spawn drops 5 kg Pokeshell Molt, while an adult Pokeshell drops 10 kg Pokeshell Molt.The chance of laying an Pinch Roe egg increases when not dwelling in either Water or Ethanol of substantial mass.


=== Oakshell ===
 →  → 
An Oakshell sheds an Oakshell Molt when transitioning to an adult. On death, an Oakshell spawn drops 100 kg Oakshell Molt, while an adult Oakshell drops 500 kg Oakshell Molt. When a baby Oakshell matures into an adult, they additionally molt 50kg. In addition, happy, well-fed adult Oakshells sheds 100 kg Oakshell Molt per cycle provided it can path to a tile without Ethanol. The chance of laying an Oak Pinch Roe increases when any Pokeshell variant dwells in Ethanol of substantial mass.

Oakshells must be happy to molt their shells, meaning a Aquatic Critter Condo will not suffice for a Tame Ungroomed Oakshell.


==== Ethanol Loop ====
A happy, well-fed, adult Oakshell produces about 100 kg/cycle from its regular molts. If ranching tame Oakshells and assuming 14 of its 15 eggs are also Oakshell morphs that mature into adults, their excess eggs contribute an additional 88.4 kg/cycle in drops.
Oakshell molts can be crushed into Wood  at a Rock Crusher, then processed in an Ethanol Distiller to produce Ethanol  , Polluted Dirt , and Carbon Dioxide .
Taking into account the extra polluted dirt from the distiller, a single Oakshell over its lifetime effectively consumes only 7.2 kg/cycle of Polluted Dirt  to yield:

94.2 kg/cycle of Ethanol  
17.5 kg/cycle of Sand 
31.4 kg/cycle of Carbon Dioxide 
189 kcal/cycle of Raw Shellfish
In other words, it converts polluted dirt into Ethanol   at 1310%, and into Sand  at 243%. The resulting ethanol and other byproducts can then be used for many applications.


===== With Critter Condo =====
With just a Critter Condo, the extra +1 happiness is enough to tip polluted dirt consumption to about neutral. A well-fed Oakshell at +5 Happiness produces 19 eggs. Assuming 18 are also Oakshell morphs that mature into adults, their excess eggs contribute 113.7 kg/cycle in drops.
Under these conditions, a single Oakshell nets the following through the distiller loop:

106.8 kg/cycle of Ethanol  
17.5 kg/cycle of Sand 
35.6 kg/cycle of Carbon Dioxide 
1.2 kg/cycle of Polluted Dirt 
240 kcal/cycle of Raw Shellfish


===== With Critter Condo and Critter Fountain =====
In the most favorable conditions of +10 Happiness (Grooming Station, Critter Fountain and Brackene, and Critter Condo), a well-fed Oakshell instead produces 37 eggs. Assuming 35 are also Oakshell morphs that mature into adults, their excess eggs contribute 221 kg/cycle in drops. 
Under these conditions, a single Oakshell nets the following through the distiller loop:

160.5 kg/cycle of Ethanol  
17.5 kg/cycle of Sand 
53.5 kg/cycle of Carbon Dioxide 
37 kg/cycle of Polluted Dirt 
467 kcal/cycle of Raw Shellfish


==== Brackene Production ====
Brackene can be used to feed Critters in order to keep them happy, meaning this is a cyclical for Oakshells as their Wood can be used to make Ethanol which can be used to grow Nosh Sprout.
2 happy adult fed Oakshell shedding its molt will produce enough Ethanol to irrigate 5 Nosh Sprouts.
That's 60 Nosh Bean per 21 cycles, which can supply 120 uses of Critter Fountain. Enough to keep 5 Critters groomed and happy.


==== Power production ====
A happy adult fed Oakshell sheds an Oakshell Molt worth 100 kg of Wood every cycle; here are the results of that molt.

When feeding this wood into a Wood Burner will produce 41.6 W of power (62.5 W if Tuned), 17.5 kg of Sand, and 14.1 kg of Carbon Dioxide.
When feeding this wood into a Ethanol Distiller then a Petroleum Generator will produce 43.3 W of Power (85 W if Tuned), 17.5 kg of Sand, 18.7 kg of Polluted Water, 29.1 kg of Carbon Dioxide, 33.3 kg of Polluted Dirt. Since it effectively makes half of the Polluted Dirt it consumes, this is an insanely efficient process that results in a lot of positive resources.
If your goal is Sand production, cooking the Polluted Dirt will result in 72.5% conversation ratio compared to other Pokeshells.
Alternatively, endlessly refeeding the Polluted Dirt to an Oakshells would result in a 33.3% Sand conversion rate, which is better than the apparent 25% advertised, but not as good at the 50% of other Pokeshells.
Compared to a Sage Hatch consuming 37 kg of Polluted Dirt to create Coal for a Coal Generator, it would produce 37 W of power (55.5 W if tuned, and 740 g of Carbon Dioxide.
Another consideration is that a Domestic Arbor Tree setup is generally -7.5 kg negative per tree in Polluted Water, as Feeding Oakshells is 18.7 kg positive; You would need 1 Oakshell per ~2.5 Arbor Trees to cancel the water loss. Since Oakshells only require an effective 37 kg of Polluted Dirt per cycle, this process is still incredibly Polluted Dirt Positive (+252 kg per set of 1 Oakshell and 2.5 Arbor Trees).
Note that additional Molts are generated from Oakshells becoming adults and dying.


=== Sanishell ===
 →  → 
Sanishells consumes Polluted Dirt, Slime, or Rot Pile and excretes Sand. The Sanishell does not produce any shells, but instead occasionally removes 888.8 germs a second from nearby tiles provided they are in liquid. This cleaning action can occur at most once every 30 seconds. On death, both Sanishell spawns and adult Sanishells drop 4,000 kcal of Raw Shellfish which can be cooked into 6,400 kcal of Cooked Seafood. The chance of laying a Sani Pinch Roe egg increases when dwelling in Water of substantial mass.


==== Morph Breeding ====
Sanishells consume significantly less mass than other critter morphs, which can be leveraged to produce Pokeshell and Oakshell eggs at a reduced diet cost by dwelling in the correct environment. This is further amplified through additional happiness bonuses like through the Aquatic Critter Condo and Aquatic Critter Fountain.


=== Breeding Morphs ===
The volume of liquid required to change a Pokeshell's reproduction chance is 350 kg. The is the same level at which buildings flood. To operate, the Grooming Station must be placed out of the liquid, meaning the Pokeshells spend some of their time not in liquid. Due to how egg-chance mechanics work, there is always a non-zero chance for any Pokeshell morph to produce a default Pinch Roe, even under continuous submersion in Ethanol   or Water  . Starting from the correct base morph and assuming uninterrupted submersion, the cycle count needed for the probability of laying a critter morph roe egg is approximately:
80% correct egg chance: ~ 3.60 cycles
90% correct egg chance: ~ 8.22 cycles
95% correct egg chance: ~ 12.85 cycles
99% correct-egg chance: ~ 23.57 cycles
99.9% correct egg chance: ~ 38.93 cycles
99.99% correct egg chance: ~ 54.28 cycles
If eggs are laid every 6 cycles, then an upper bound on the correct number of eggs laid across its life span is 14.76 eggs out of 15, or 98.4%. 

As a result, all Oakshell/Sanishell ranches will produce some Pokeshells, and automated systems should account for this. On the other hand, Pokeshell ranches will never produce Oakshell or Sanishell roe provided they don't enter substantial water or ethanol. A small layer of liquid to prevent any offgassing will not change their reproduction chance if kept under 350 kg. 


== Feeding troubles ==
Rot Piles, Slime and Polluted Dirt are messy food sources, sublimating into Polluted Oxygen and thus naturally uncommon and transitory. Which makes feeding domestic Pokeshells quite a task.  Note, however, that groomed Pokeshells will live long enough to reproduce once even if not fed. As their laying rate is the same whether fed or not (as long as they're tame and groomed), ranches of unfed, but groomed, Pokeshells can be quite efficient (though you'll need to feed them to increase the size or quantity of those ranches)


=== Ethanol Distiller ===
Ethanol Distillers provide a reliable source of Polluted Dirt. Since each Pokeshell needs 116 g/s of Polluted Dirt, an Ethanol Distiller running can feed nearly 3 domesticated Pokeshells.


=== Water Sieve ===
A Water Sieve produces small amount of Polluted Dirt when purifying Polluted Water and is commonly found cleaning lavatories.  However, not even a constantly running Water Sieve is enough to feed one Pokeshell.


=== Rotting food with Polluted Water ===
Pokeshells can be used as a garbage disposal for getting rid of any unsightly food debris. Since food items weigh very little, this method is not feasible for maintaining fed Pokeshells.


=== Outhouse Cleanup ===
Pokeshells can be used to eat up polluted dirt emptied from outhouses to supply sand for deodorizer, serving as a medium for temporary clean oxygen solution in remote regions, or during early game. For each cycle, all Outhouses in a room needs to be visited by Duplicants at least 8 times in sum and emptied timely to satiate a Pokeshell. They can be kept in their innoctous mode for decacycles before laying an egg  (critters typically lay eggs by 2/3 of their life; check their age to avoid putting an egg-laying prone crab in dupe's frequent outhouse). However, once a Pinch Roe is laid, it's imperative to send dupes to attack the angry pokeshell in protecting mode to prevent harm.


=== Keeping crabs wild ===
A reasonable alternative to domesticating Pokeshell is simply to wrangle all the wild Pokeshell in the map to a single room of decent size where they will remain a perpetual source of Pokeshell Molt for a supplemental amount of Lime. Be careful to disallow access to this room using door permissions so duplicants do not accidentally run into a mass of murderous Pokeshells if there are any Pokeshell eggs in the room.
Once domestication time comes, it is still better to start with one Pokeshell, and keep the rest of wild population self-sustaining.


== Tips ==
The roof or floor segments made out of unpassable Pneumatic Doors can help with the safe egg extraction.
 Feeding Pokeshells with Polluted Dirt is easier in the DLC, due to the existence of asteroid types that have a lot of Polluted Dirt seams.

The Saturn Critter Trap is a carnivorous food plant found in the Radioactive Biome that eats small land critters and expel Hydrogen.


== Seed ==
The Saturn Critter Trap can only be found in the Radioactive Biome either as a living plant or as a buried object. This plant has no seed chance and therefore can not be mutated. Seeds are limited and cannot be obtained through farming or through the Printing Pod, but can be obtained by exchanging 25 Data Banks at the Printerceptor story trait.

Saturn Critter Traps produce 12,000 kcal of Plant Meat every 30 cycles or about 400 kcal a cycle. Although comparable to other crop plants for calories, Plant Meat only has a Food Quality of +1 and is not an ingredient to better food recipes.  It can however be fed to Sage Hatches which can then be ranched for meat.


== Hydrogen Production ==
While growing, the Saturn Critter Trap produces Hydrogen. The Hydrogen is produced and stored internally at a rate of 167g every 4 seconds (25kg per cycle / 41.667g/s) at a temperature +10 °C / +18 °F higher than its body temperature. The plant vents its stored Hydrogen into the environment once it reaches 33.25 kg of Hydrogen. This rate of Hydrogen production is the same for both wild and domesticated plants and unaffected by growth buffs such as Farmer's Touch.
The Saturn Critter Trap must be growing to produce Hydrogen. When growth is stopped due to environmental conditions or lack of a critter to eat, no new Hydrogen is produced, but currently stored Hydrogen is unaffected.
Each Saturn Critter Trap being fed constantly can support 0.41667 Hydrogen Generator, and each Hydrogen Generator requires 2.4 Saturn Critter Trap fed constantly.

The Saturn Critter Traps require cold temperature range of -90.1 °C ↔ -0.1 °C / -130.18 °F ↔ 31.82 °F and ignore atmospheric pressure. Saturn Critter Traps require a small, land critter to eat every harvest.


=== Wild ===
A wild Saturn Critter Trap takes 120 cycles to grow to maturity.


=== Domestic ===
The Saturn Critter Trap can be planted in a Planter Box, a Farm Tile, or a Hydroponic Farm. It needs to be fertilized with 10 kg/cycle of Polluted Water   .


== Saturn Critter Trap Edible Critters ==
Saturn Critter Traps eat only small, land critters and will not eat other critters. This includes flying critters like Shine Bug, Puft, and Gassy Moo, aquatic critters like Pacu, and large critters like Bammoth.
Beetiny are an efficient source to fed Saturn Critter Traps due to Beeta Hive being a consistent source of Beetiny without any input.

The Shine Bug is a critter found in the Sandstone Biome. They emit light without creating heat, and provide a small decor bonus. They can be domesticated, and produce Shine Nymph Eggs when captive. 

 All Shine Bugs give off Radiation, 60 Rads at the tile they occupy, with a radius of 6 tiles (including the central tile.) There is no difference in the amount of radiation given off by the different Shine Bug morphs.


== Behavior ==
Shine Bugs are relatively rare, with two or three spawning in the temperate biome. They are commonly found in places with lots of Mealwood, Bristle Blossoms, Bluff Briars, and Muckroots. They can drown in water and can be killed by attacking them.
Shine Bugs are quite lonely critters, as only a few exist in the asteroid, so they constantly seek each other, and sometimes mistake Duplicant-made lighting as new friends, bobbing up and down in greeting. They are, however, attracted to things emitting light, and are more likely to move towards things such as lamps, light bulbs, or other Shine Bugs. Shine bugs will consume any Gristle Berry or Bristle Berry that is found lying around. They seem oblivious to the atmosphere in which they're kept, although temperature extremes will prove lethal to them.


== Critter Morphs ==
Shine bugs enjoy the largest array of critter morphs that can be unlocked through Ranching, each critter morph requiring a different foodstuff and providing a progressively increased decor benefit. They must be raised successively, with each generation providing a chance to produce the next when provided with the correct foodstuff.
They are as follows:

 →  → 
The original variant consumes Bristle Berry, Gristle Berry and Phosphorite. They provide illumination and moderately improve decor (+30) in a modest 5 tile radius. They are short lived, but reproduce quickly with a 67% per cycle reproduction rate when tamed and fed. If fed Gristle Berry, they have an increased chance of producing Sun Nymph eggs.
Shine Bugs emit light at 1800 Lux while uncrowded.

Sun Bugs emit light at 1800 Lux while uncrowded.

== Tips ==


=== Resin Production ===
Shine Bug eggs can be cracked at an Egg Cracker to produce 5 kg of Resin   . Note that eggs deteriorating in storage due to 0% viability do not drop any Resin. On some asteroid starts, this is the earliest way for a player to acquire wood building material which is needed to construct Communal Tables, Hot Tubs, and Saunas.
This is also technically an early source of Plastic , although considerable time and effort is needed to produce enough to construct something useful - if a happy Shine Bug lays 13 eggs in its lifetime and 1 is used for replenishing the stable, then it effectively produces about 2.4 kg/cycle of Resin or 1.4 kg/cycle of Plastic. A full, 16 shine bug stable produces about 23 kg/cycle which is enough to construct a Steam Turbine in 8.68 cycles. For perspective, a single Glossy Drecko can be sheared for 50 kg/cycle and produces enough for a Steam Turbine in 4 cycles.


=== Shine Bug Decor Farming ===
Shine Bug ranches with Window Tiles as ceiling and floor can be placed near areas that would benefit from high Decor, such as Great Hall and Recreational Room, or areas with a large source of Decor penalty (such as Heavi-Watt Wire).
To make the Decor bonus from Shine Bugs more consistent, place a Lamp or a Ceiling Light at one side and a Critter Feeder on the other side.
All variants between Sun Bug and Azure Bug have the same Decor bonus, so the excess of these Shine Bugs can be allowed to roam around the base, as long as they cannot enter areas with extreme temperatures or areas that must be kept dark, such as bedrooms and Dusk Cap farms.
The Abyss Bug variant doesn't emit light, so it can be worthwhile to set up a dedicated ranch for Abyss Bugs to boost Decor in rooms that must be kept dark.


=== Radiant Bug Breeding ===


==== Initial Breeding ====
Shine Bugs reproduce quickly (2 eggs every 3 cycles), so just feeding all Shine Bugs with Phosphorite  allows breeding up to Abyss Bugs in around 50 cycles.
Feeding variants with their respective specialized diet can greatly accelerate this process, but requires more management.
Make sure to remove eggs from the stable to prevent the cramped debuff from slowing down egg production.
It is recommended to keep a separate stable of Abyss Bugs fed off a diet of Abyssalite  before moving on the Radiant Bug variant, in order to boost Decor in places that must be kept dark.


==== Feeding Radiant Bugs ====
Radiant Bugs can eat 1 kg of Diamond  or 1 kg (4000 kcal) of Barbeque per cycle. If both are in short supply, Shove Voles can be ranched for large amounts of meat.
Note that Barbeque production can occupy an Electric Grill for a large amount of time.
To prevent Barbeque spoilage, limit the Critter Feeder storage to 8 kg or lower, or maintain Deep Freeze and Sterile Atmosphere environments.
Alternatively, feed Abyss Bugs with Barbeque temporarily to increase the Radiant Bug Egg chance, then switch back to Abyssalite  to save on Barbeque. This involves considerable user intervention.


==== Distribution and Decor Boost ====
Excess Radiant Bugs can be distributed to places that would benefit from high Decor, as mentioned above. Radiant Bugs can produce exceptionally high Decor compared to other variants.
When Radiant Bugs are distributed in kitchen areas, they may consume fresh Barbeque if it is not stored quickly.


=== Medicine Herding ===
Sun Bugs can be bred to produce Sun Bug Eggs, which can then be used to produce Serum Vial, which cures Zombie Spores.


=== Shine Bug Reactor Farming ===

Shove Voles are Critters that live on the surface of the asteroid. They can burrow through most tiles and climb on walls and ceilings. However, they cannot burrow through tiles made of refined metal or those made from materials with a hardness exceeding 150, such as Abyssalite, Insulite, Wolframite, Diamond, Neutronium, and Obsidian. They also cannot burrow through the Gravitas Door or Pneumatic Door of any material type.


== Behaviour ==
They eat debris and excrete it as a solid tile but at a 50% loss of mass, renewing the asteroid's surface after meteors hit and destroy it. At least 240 kg of material must be consumed before they poop.
When meteor showers begin, they automatically burrow, only resurfacing once the bombardment phase is over. This behavior prevents Shove Voles from taking damage from dangerous meteors.
Shove Voles have a personal space requirement of 0, and thus will never feel Cramped or Crowded.
Shove Voles cannot be confined.
Shove Voles may drown in liquids, but will completely ignore liquids during pathfinding as long as the destination cell is one they won’t drown in.

== Domestication ==
Care should be taken when bringing them into a sub-surface stable as a source of meat.
Once unleashed into the asteroid, it is difficult to track them down, steel airlocks or Pneumatic Doors as the sole access are advised as well as metal or obsidian tiles wherever abyssalite is missing, plus Robo-Miners if you feed them. Note that airlocks have to be built from steel, as shove voles will pass through airlocks built from Copper Ore, Aluminum Ore or Iron Ore; pneumatic doors can safely be built out of any material.
Wrangling can occasionally be finnicky, as they may frequently travel to areas your duplicant cannot access and interrupt their task. Critter Traps can be useful here to avoid this behavior.
While they may be able to burrow, they can not fly or use ladders. If space is not an issue, building a platform with a 2-tile wide gap separating it from other walls can stop Voles from escaping. However, the eggs that drop down still need to be collected and placed back on platform.

Shove voles are an almost fully sustainable food source that does not require feeding. One vole will provide 1075 kcal/cycle of meat or 1344 kcal/cycle of barbeque provided the eggs are incubated and voles are groomed.
A vole takes 4 cycles to incubate, 5 cycles to mature, and 6 cycles to produce an egg. Total time to produce an egg : 4+5+6 = 15 cycles
Or, without incubators, 20 cycles to incubate, 5 cycles to mature, and 6 cycles to produce an egg. Total time to produce an egg : 20+5+6 = 31 cycles

A tamed vole will start with 43,200 kcal upon hatching. Note: Delecta Voles start with fewer calories and will starve before producing an egg, if tamed.

Because they drop so much meat (and thus barbeque) they can be used as an alternative food source for radiant bugs if diamond is in short supply or unavailable.

Sleet Wheat is a cold dwelling plant found in the Frozen Biome; it produces Sleet Wheat Grain. Sleet Wheat Grain is both a food item and the seed for planting more Sleet Wheat. Sleet Wheat is very slow to mature, at 18 cycles, and combined with the temperature requirements, the colony needs to have a well established infrastructure before it can be effectively farmed.
Sleet Wheat Grain is needed to make Frost Buns (and thus Frost Burgers), Pepper Bread, Soufflé Pancakes, and Berry Sludge.
In all recipes that require it, Sleet Wheat Grain can be substituted by an equal amount of Megafrond Grain. 
In most recipes, each Sleet Wheat grain is worth 400 kcal when prepared.
The plant is notable for its unusual seed mechanics: Sleet Wheat Grain is both the product and the seed.


== Fertilization ==


== Food ==
It produces 18 Sleet Wheat Grains per harvest which can be processed into Frost Bun and Soufflé Pancakes at an Electric Grill, Pepper Bread at a Gas Range, or Berry Sludge at a Microbe Musher.
Frost Bun provides 1200 kcals and requires 3 Sleet Wheat Grains.

(1200 kcals / 3 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles) / 1 plant = 400 kcals / cycle / plant
A Duplicant requires ~1000 kcals per cycle. So you need 1000/400 = 2.5 plants per dupe.
Soufflé Pancakes provide 3600 kcals and requires 2 Sleet Wheat Grains and 1600 kcal of Raw Egg. The Raw Egg is given the same value as an Omelette in this calculation, of 2800 kcal. That, plus the standard amount of calories in 2 Sleet Wheat Grains (400 per grain x 2 grains = 800), gives us 3600.

(800 kcals / 2 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 Cycles) / 1 plant = 400 kcals / cycle / plant
With 1 plant at 400 kcals, you need 0.56 plants per dupe.
You would also need 444 kcal per dupe of Raw Egg.
Berry Sludge provides 4000 kcals and requires 5 Sleet Wheat Grains. It improves food quality to Good(+3) with additional requirement of Bristle Blossom to be planted.  Since 1600kcal (1 berry) of Bristle Berry is required, it's net caloric gain is 2400kcal

(2400 kcals / 5 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles) / 1 plant = 480 kcals / cycle / plant
1 Bristle Berry / 6 cycles * 6 plants and 18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles * 5 plants allows for the production of 18 berry sludge per 18 cycles.
So you need 1000 (kcals / dupe) / 800 (Berry Sludge kcal / 5 Sleet Wheat plants) = 1.25 plants per dupe.  Since Bristle Berry is also necessary at a 6:5 ratio, you will also need 1.25*1.2 = 1.5 Bristle Berry plants per dupe. It is worth mentioning that this entire process is fairly power intensive.
Pepper Bread provides 4000 kcals and requires 10 Sleet Wheat Grains. It improves food quality to Superb(+5) with additional requirement of Pincha Pepper to be planted.

(4000 kcals / 10 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles) / 1 plant = 400 kcals / cycle / plant
So you need 1000/400 = 2.5 plants per dupe.
Mixed Berry Pie provides 4200 kcals and requires 3 Sleet Wheat Grains, 1000 kcals of Grubfruit and 2000 kcals of Gristle Berry. It has food quality of Superb (+5) and spoil time of 4 cycles. Overall caloric gain from Grubfruit and Gristle Berry is 1200 kcals and 400 kcals per Grain, which is the same as Frost Bun.

(1200 kcals / 3 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles) / 1 plant = 400 kcals / cycle / Sleet Wheat plant
A standard Duplicant requires ~1000 kcals per cycle. So you need 1000/400 = 2.5 Sleet Wheat plants per dupe.
Frost Burger provides 6000 kcals and requires 1200 kcals of Frost Bun. It improves food quality to Ambrosial(+6) with additional requirement of Waterweed to be planted.

(6000 kcals / 3 Sleet Wheat Grains) * (18 Sleet Wheat Grains / 18 cycles) / 1 plant = 2000 kcals / cycle / plant
So you need 1000/2000 = 0.5 plants per dupe.


== Growth ==

A Sleet Wheat requires temperature range of -55 °C ↔ 5 °C / -67 °F ↔ 41 °F, and air pressure of 150 g ↔ 10000 g. It requires atmosphere of Oxygen, Polluted Oxygen or Carbon Dioxide. 


=== Wild ===
A wild Sleet Wheat takes 72 cycles to grow.


=== Domestic ===
It can be planted in a Planter Box, a Farm Tile or a Hydroponic Farm.
It requires 5 kg/cycle Dirt and 20 kg/cycle Water.
A domestic Sleet Wheat takes 18 cycles to grow.


=== Spoilage ===
Unlike all other foods and ingredients, Sleet Wheat Grain is Deep Frozen below 10 °C and Refrigerated below 35 °C. 
Sleet Wheat Grain will spoil in Oxygen or Polluted Oxygen. Although Sleet Wheat grows just fine in Oxygen or Polluted Oxygen, when it matures and drops its Sleet Wheat Grain,  it will start to spoil if not picked up. Therefore, in the early game, it is advised to ensure that any wild sleet wheat is covered in carbon dioxide to avoid spoilage.

== Tips ==
Since Berry Sludge is extremely useful  for rocket trips (it doesn't spoil), and Sleet Wheat is difficult to farm in the early game, it is strongly advised to keep and harvest any wild sleet wheat found on the starting asteroid.
For beginners, it is recommended to plant Sleet Wheat in Planter Boxes or Farm Tiles rather than Hydroponic Farms as the pumped water can turn into ice and damage pipes if below -0.6 °C / 30.92 °F or warm up the farm above growth threshold. Whilst hydroponic farms require less maintenance, players should first practice how to cool water to a specific temperature to prevent pipe breakages (e.g. thermal sensors deactivating Wheezewort built on doors).
If warm water is used for irrigation the air surrounding the Sleet Wheat needs to be constantly cooled. This can be achieved using Wheezewort.
Liquid Valves, when set slightly below Sleet Wheat's consumption rate, can be used to minimize the amount of water idly sitting in the pipes. Each 3 Sleet Wheat tiles require 100 grams of water per second. (Care should be taken with this setup to maintain the growth rate and evenly distribute water without stumbling over internal buffers.)
Sleet Wheat farms are inherently resistant to spoilage and Food Poisoning, since they require such cold temperatures.
Using a Fertilizer Synthesizer and Farm Station increases the overall dirt efficiency of the farm, although it requires the addition of Phosphorite.
The used Dirt temperatures affects the plants. To avoid heating up, store them inside a Storage Bin submerged in cold Polluted Water or similar.
If Frost Bun is seen as the base line amount of Calories, 1200 / 3, then each Sleet Wheat Grain provides 400 kcals.
This means that the net caloric gain of Berry Sludge and Frost Burger is +400 kcals. Pepper Bread and Mixed Berry Pie is +0 kcals.
Sleet Wheat with Frost Bun provide a baseline 400 Calories per day, if the plants drop instead of being harvested it decreases to 327.
Pepper Bread does not increase the effective kcal, meaning it remains 400 and 327 respectively.
Overall, the Sleet Wheat Farm should be either well insulated using Insulated Tiles or placed in a Frozen Biome.

Slickster is a critter found in Oil Biome. They consume large quantities of Carbon Dioxide and turn it to Crude Oil. The longhair variant consumes Oxygen and produce nothing but +50 decor in 7 tile  radius.


== Behavior ==


=== Diet ===
Slicksters consume 20 kg/cycle (33 g/s) of Carbon Dioxide and output 50% of consumed mass as Crude Oil / Petroleum at their body temperature, it's almost heat-neutral, with some mass creation in the petroleum case.


=== Space Requirements ===
Slicksters of all types require 12 open squares per slickster to avoid feeling overcrowded. 


=== Temperature Preference ===
Due to their high mass (400 kg), and replacing a gas with low thermal conductivity with a liquid with a high one at their body temperature, they tend to change temperature rather slowly. This at first can be beneficial, as they will take a while in a room temperature area to cool down, but it can make it very difficult to warm them back up to prevent longhair eggs and keep them comfortable. A Liquid Tepidizer can easily provide an adequate temperature for them even without automation, and can simply be submerged in their crude oil output.


=== Movement ===
Slicksters move by hovering, They move over solid ground as a Hatch would, but treat tiles with sufficient quantity of liquid (> 1000 kg) as if they were solid. They can jump 1 and 2 tile up/down diagonally, and between 1 tile gap. They can wiggle and swim in water or polluted water mist above liquids, and in shallow liquid surface (<1000 kg) as long as it's not forming a tile. They fall and drown when the tile-forming liquid they just arrived at has pressure <1000 kg.  When drowning, they will try to reach the surface and land on the nearest dense tile exposed to air. Since they have no learning memories, drowning once at a place won't teach them not going to the same spot next time. If there is an air-exposed tile in their reachable path, drowning is self-resolvable and not an issue to worry about.


== Critter Morphs ==
The Slickster has three variants, each with its own varied diet and temperature preferences.


=== Slickster ===
 →  →  
The Slickster is the purple variant and often found near the bottom of the map. Converts Carbon Dioxide into Crude Oil.


=== Longhair Slickster ===
 →  →  
A lower-temperature variant with a decor bonus. Consumes Oxygen (30 kg/cycle, or 50 g/sec) and produces nothing. Acts as an expensive pet (there is a +50 Decor bonus from the Longhair Slickster).
A longhair slickster egg has an increased chance of laying when the slickster's body temperature range is 20 °C ↔ 60 °C / 68 °F ↔ 140 °F.
Can help curb oxygen overproduction with obligate 100% uptime SPOM (that is, one whose excess energy production is used to power other critical buildings, this dependency is not recommended and typically avoided). Two happy, tame longhair slicksters consume as much oxygen as one duplicant.
Colonies with stable Oxygen production can benefit from ranching Longhair Slicksters as an alternative to Shine Bug morphs. Unlike most tame critters, Longhair Slicksters can still be easily fed outside of a dedicated ranch, and the Decor they produce is not affected by their metabolism- as tame, glum critters only have 20% of their normal metabolism, ungroomed longhairs placed in areas of your base that Duplicants will spend reasonable amounts of time in (such as dining halls or recreation rooms) can provide a substantial increase to environmental Decor without taking up additional Building space, while only consuming a tenth of the oxygen as a Duplicant. As they will not starve as long as they are kept in Oxygen, they will even sustain their own population by laying a single egg during their lifetime, which, due to their longer lifespans compared to the other morphs, is all but guaranteed to be another Longhair if the ambient temperature isn't too hot.
Can also be ranched for meat if for some reason a colony runs out of food to feed hatches (and their variants) with and there is abundant oxygen production capacity from renewable water sources and SPOM. Though, their only advantage over say renewable drecko meat (balm lily, and produces meat at same rate) is ease of ranching (they don't climb on walls).
An interesting proposition, due to the advent of geo-tuning and industrial bleach stone production, is that water producing geysers produce significant amounts of power when fully geo-tuned (matching or even beating that of fully geo-tuned steam vents), but only if their (immense) output can be directed elsewhere. Since venting valuable resources, such as water, into space is ethically dubious, longhair slickster ranching can be used to convert this excess water production into meat while ensuring power production from geo-tuned geysers.

Puft is a non-aggressive critter that breathes in certain gasses (depending on their variation: Polluted Oxygen, Oxygen, and Chlorine) and excretes them as their solid counterparts (Slime, Oxylite, and Bleach Stone, respectively).


== Behavior ==
Pufts search for the nearest element to inhale. The baseline is to consume 500 g every second for 3 seconds, but can inhale for up to 15 seconds depending on how hungry the Puft is. Exceptionally hungry Pufts will inhale for the full 15 seconds as well as consume additional mass.
Pufts are non-hostile and will flee when attacked.
Puft eggs take 15 cycles to hatch outside of an Incubator, or 3 cycles if Lullabied.


== Critter Morphs ==
Pufts have 4 critter morphs. Pufts in the same room as a Puft Prince increases the chance of laying a Dense Puft or Squeaky Puff egg, and decreases the chance of laying a Puft Prince egg. Pufts not in the same room as a Puft Prince increases the chance of laying a Puft Prince egg.


=== Puft ===
 →  → 
The Puft that is the yellow, three-eyed critter most often encountered in the wild. It ingests Polluted Oxygen and excretes Slime with 95% efficiency (i.e. the mass of the excreted slime is 95% that of the inhaled Polluted Oxygen).
The Slime can used to farm Dusk Caps or converted to Algae (Algae Distiller) or Phyto Oil (Plant Pulverizer).
The Puft can lay all four kinds of eggs (94% chance Puft, 2% chance of other morphs), depending if there is a Puft Prince nearby and its age. 

The chance of laying a Puft egg will decrease over time no matter what it's penned with.
If not penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Puft Prince eggs will increase over time.
If penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Dense Puft and Squeaky Puft eggs will increase over time.
Pufts pair well with Morbs, since they will consume the Polluted Oxygen that the Morb produces.


=== Puft Prince ===
 →  → 
The Puft Prince is otherwise the same as the basic Puft variant, but can breathe all three gases, though only excreting 10% of the inhaled mass. They are, however, needed to get Pufts to produce eggs for the Dense Puft and Squeaky Puft variations.
Puft Prince can only lay Puft eggs, as the Puft Prince is always stabled with itself, and its initial 2% chance to lay a Puft Prince Egg will disappear before it can lay one.


=== Dense Puft ===
 →  → 
The Dense Puft requires Oxygen and creates Oxylite at 95% efficiency.
The produced Oxylite can be used as an oxydizer in Rockets.
Dense Puft can lay Puft (31%), Puft Prince (2%), and Dense Puft (67%) eggs.

If not penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Puft Prince eggs will increase over time.
If penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Dense Puft eggs will increase over time.
The chance of laying a Puft egg will decrease over time no matter what it's penned with, but changes much slower than the other two.


=== Squeaky Puft ===
 →  → 
The Squeaky Puft requires Chlorine and creates Bleach Stone at 95% efficiency.
The produced Bleach Stone can be used to farm Waterweed or refill Hand Sanitizers.
Squeaky Puft can lay Puft (31%), Puft Prince (2%), and Squeaky Puft (67%) eggs.

If not penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Puft Prince eggs will increase over time.
If penned with Puft Prince, the chance of laying Squeaky Puft eggs will increase over time.
The chance of laying a Puft egg will decrease over time no matter what it's penned with, but changes much slower than the other two.


== Puft Ranching ==
The main issue with puft ranching is necessity to keep liquid on the floor of their enclosure to keep outputs in solid form, and regularly sort out their eggs into dedicated enclosures. 


=== Slime farm ===
Building a stable room with Polluted Water on the floor and filling it with plain Pufts is enough. Water will off-gas Polluted Oxygen, feeding pufts. It may be easier to keep the population of Pufts higher by keeping a separate Puft Prince stable to produce Puft eggs.
With Spaced Out, a single Sublimation Station running continuously was enough to feed just under 8 Pufts.
Morbs can be used to produce Polluted Oxygen with no costs after setting it up, and at a cheap price. Each puft requires roughly 4.2 morbs.
Slime can be used to grow Mushrooms sustainably or converted into Algae.


=== Oxylite farm ===
The basic setup for Dense Puft will be the same as for plain Puft, but with Deodorizers. More advanced ones will require constant input of oxygen from the outside.
Compared with Oxylite Refinery, this approach requires no power and produces no heat.
To get the Dense Pufts, ranch normal Pufts with a Puft Prince and you'll have a 50% chance of the right egg dropping. To keep the ranch going, a single Puft Prince will keep Dense Pufts producing their own eggs.


=== Bleach Stone farm ===
The goal of this setup is to produce Bleach Stone with Squeaky Pufts. Squeaky Pufts are a renewable source of Bleach Stone, which makes them an option for sustainable geotuning. Every Geyser that produces some form of Water (such as the Cool Steam Vent) requires Bleach Stone to geotune, 25g/s on average. This means that a single Squeaky Puft can support almost 2 geotuners.
Chlorine is usually abundant and can be renewably sourced from a Chlorine Gas Vent. Each vent can support about 2 Squeaky Pufts. This setup will require a bit more than the basic Slime or Oxylite setups, due to the 60 °C / 140 °F Chlorine environment. Build a stable room with the vent inside, covering the floor with enough water to prevent the Bleach Stone from sublimating. Airlocks and Atmo Suits are recommended, as well as Insulated Tile to prevent the heat from bleeding into the surrounding area. In addition, make sure there aren't any other gasses in the room, as Pufts tend to float while Chlorine sinks.
