Divergent is the term for the two different variants of a single Critter species, those being Sweetles and Grubgrubs. While visually very different, one can lay the egg of the other. Both varieties can be found in the Wasteland Biome, along with Spindly Grubfruit Plants.


== Behavior ==
Sweetles and Grubgrubs pollinate Plants on the ground level (including those in Farm Tiles and Planter Boxes, but not in Flower Pots), giving them Pollinated: Sweetle (+5% Growth Speed) or Pollinated: Grubgrub (+50% Growth Speed) for 1 cycle. Pollination has a cooldown of 75 seconds. The growth boost is the same whether the critter is wild or tame. Pollinators do not try to pollinate plants that are already pollinated, making the effects not stackable. While well-fed, divergents tend to about 8 plants per cycle; when hungry, they tend to about 4 per cycle.
Pollination from a Divergent is the only way to convert a Spindly Grubfruit Plant into a Grubfruit Plant.

Sweetle will not retaliate when attacked. Grubgrub, however, will deal 4-6 damage in retaliation when a Duplicant attacks. Typically, it can only manage one attack on a Duplicant, but if multiple Duplicants attack at once, they can all remain unharmed.


== Critter Morphs ==
Divergents have an increased chance to lay Grubgrub eggs if allowed to pollinate Grubfruit Plants. While both are able to eventually lay Grubgrub eggs with 99% chance after pollinating enough Grubfruit Plant, Grubgrubs have a higher initial egg chance of 67% while the initial chance for Sweetles is 2%. Grubgrub eggs chances increase by about 2.5% per Pollinated (Sweetle), with subsequent pollinations being less effective.


=== Sweetle ===
 →  → 
Sweetles require 12 cells each in a ranch to not be overcrowded. A 96-Tile Stable can house 8 Sweetles.


=== Grubgrub ===
 →  → 
Grubgrub require 16 cells each in a ranch to not be overcrowded. A 96-tile Stable can house 6 Grubgrubs.


== Tips ==
Sweetle are one of the few remaining critters which can be starvation ranched without grooming. A tame Sweetle with enough space will lay one egg before starving to death. If it is groomed, it will lay two eggs before starving. This allows for a population to be maintained or grown even in the absence of providing any food. Do note that an ungroomed population will slowly lose 2% each generation due to eggs naturally hatching as Grubgrubs.
Sweetles enable sustainable creation of Sucrose. To maximize Sucrose production. Care should be taken if kept in a ranch with Grubfruit Plant, as this can result in them laying significantly more Grubgrub. This may make it difficult to replenish a Sweetle ranch with Sweetles.
Grubgrubs are best paired with Plants to pollinate for faster growth. This can be done without feeding them until they starve, or starvation can be prevented by feeding them only once every 10 cycles.
To maximize Mud production, Grubgrubs should be fed Sucrose . Grubgrubs transform only 10% of the mass of Sulfur  into Mud  , but 100% of the mass of Sucrose into Mud. Despite the 50% loss when Sweetles convert Sulfur into Sucrose, the conversion is ultimately 5x better to have Sweetles turn Sulfur into Sucrose and then feed the Sucrose to Grubgrubs. To do that, you need a ratio of 3 fed Sweetles per Grubgrub.
To maximize the amount of calories produced per kilogram of Sulfur, it's best to ranch Sweetles with only a few Grubfruit Plants per ranches. Much of the calories will come in the form of Meat. Sweetles lay eggs faster than Grubgrubs, require less space before they become overcrowded, and eat less sulfur, but Grubgrub drop more meat upon death. Keeping Sweetles with Grubfruit Plants will maximize the chance that they will drop Grubgrub eggs which can then be turned into more Meat. If that meat is turned into Barbeque, one happy Sweetle can produce 6000 calories/4.5 cycle = 1333 calories per cycle this way. That's assuming the additional calories from Grubgrub Plants balances out the inefficiencies from occasional Sweetle eggs.
To feed the Sweetles, Grubgrubs, and Grubfruit Plants long-term requires a source of Sulfur, and so a Sulfur Geyser tamer is recommended. The high temperature of the Sulfur is a problem, and Sulfur has very low thermal conductivity that will make cooling once it's solid quite a hassle. However, since a geyser will only output less than 3 kg/s of Liquid Sulfur, the output can be pumped and then split into three pipes for cooling without solidifying in the pipes before being output.
For an average 1.5 kg/s of liquid Sulfur Geyser, 45 Sweetle can be fully fed, creating 450 kg/cycle Sucrose. If all Sucrose is used to feed Grubgrubs, 15 Grubgrubs can be fully fed, creating 450 kg/cycle Mud. which can be refined to 180 kg/cycle Dirt + 270 kg/cycle Water using a Sludge Press. That's enough for 18 Mealwood and to oxygenate 4 Duplicant using an Electrolyzer.
A Sour Gas Boiler will also produce the necessary Sulfur for long term farming of Grubgrubs and Grubfruit. Though at that stage in the game food will most likely no longer be an issue, this could be used as a source of high volume, sustainable food production for Sap production. Sour gas boilers require no external input and are fully sustainable.

Pacu is an aquatic Critter found in pools in the Swamp Biome. They produce Fish Fillets and Eggs, and their morphs can provide either fresh Water or decor bonuses. They can be domesticated.


== Behavior ==
Pacu float around in liquids at the flooding level (over 35% of default mass), and will generally otherwise be in the "flopping" state; while flopping doesn't hurt them, it gives them confined status.
They have a short lifespan of 25 cycles and a high egg mass (4 kg). This makes them very useful for food and Lime. On death, they drop 1,000 kcal of Fish Fillet, which can be cooked into 1,600 kcal of Cooked Seafood at an Electric Grill.
Their excrement can be fed to Pokeshells for additional lime, although it takes about 22 to feed each.
Unlike most critters, which need to be groomed, Pacus are tamed by feeding from a Fish Feeder, and this takes much longer, about 6.66 cycles instead of the usual 2.
A Pacu is crowded if the sum of all aquatic creatures personal space requirement in the pool exceeds the size of the pool. The critter's happiness decreases by this difference, divided by that critter's personal space requirement (rounded up).
A Pacu is cramped if the sum of all aquatic creatures and eggs personal space requirement in the pool exceeds the size of the pool, with a minimum of 1 egg.
The pool size is the number of connected, non-navigable liquid cells. A non-navigable liquid cell is either a liquid cell that exceeds 35% of its default mass, or a liquid cell with another solid/liquid cell on top. Non-navigable cells can drown non-aquatic critters. Liquid inside Mesh Tiles and Pneumatic Doors also count and are treated as one pool of liquid with the surrounding liquid.
Aquatic critters in the same room but not in the pool will not impact a Pacus Crowdedness, although the Pacus will impact the Crowdedness of the normal critters.
Unlike other critters, they will not be confined when inside an open door.

Pacus will only swim into tiles of at least 35% default mass, and have trouble swimming into liquids that are not substantial. This can be used to limit Pacu movement for performance reasons or to help them reach their feed. Pacus that are not in tile of substantial liquid begin flopping. Flopping Pacus will look for the nearest body of liquid and attempt to move in that direction. While Flopping, Pacus will fall through Pneumatic Doors and open Manual Airlocks/Mechanized Airlocks.
All Pacus have a mass of 200 kg when hatched and when they reach adulthood. Newly born Pacu have body temperatures which are specific to their variant, resulting in heat creation/deletion.


== Critter Morphs ==
The Pacu is a temperature sensitive critter with two additional variants. Provided the fish is placed in a pool of the correct temperature, it produces its variants consistently and quickly. All maintain the same behavior, and large egg mass, making the difference largely a matter of preferred temperature, as Pacu's short lifespan and high masses will greatly stabilize an area's temperature.

When Pacus hatch and reach adulthood, (which takes 5 cycles) their temperature is 30 °C / 86 °F.

The colorful Tropical Pacu is the most frequently spotted variant morph of the Pacu. The chance of laying a Tropical Fry Egg increases when a Pacu body temperature is between 35 °C ↔ 80 °C / 95 °F ↔ 176 °F. They provide a +25 decor out to a radius of 5 squares but this decor only penetrates Window Tile.
When Tropical Pacus hatch and reach adulthood, their temperature is 55 °C / 131 °F.


=== Gulp Fish ===
 →  → 
The blue Gulp Fish is the second variant of the Pacu. The chance of laying a Gulp Fish Egg increases when a Pacu body temperature is between -30 °C ↔ -5 °C / -22 °F ↔ 23 °F. They also have the drawback of requiring temperature management - too hot and they die off, too cold and the pool they are in starts to freeze. They do, however, convert Polluted Water into Water, at a slow and consistent pace of 200 g/s. A large pool filled with these critters can produce enough fresh water to support a base though water needs to be siphoned off quickly thanks to its higher freezing point than Polluted Water. Alternatively, if the Polluted Water is cold enough the water that the Gulp Fish produces will instantly freeze into Ice, which can be collected and melted.
The water that Gulp Fish produce matches their internal body temperature, which can cause massive heat creation/deletion depending on a Gulp Fish's temperature relative to the Polluted Water that it takes in.
When Gulp Fish hatch and reach adulthood, their temperature is -12.5 °C / 9.5 °F.


== Pacu Ranching ==


=== Tamed Pacu ===
A newly-born tame Pacu will live long enough to lay an egg, even when not fed, as long as it is not kept with too many other Pacu (9 in 8 tiles of liquid will work). This allows some limited starvation ranching potential, but the yield is rather low considering the investment in materials to set up systems to automatically store the starving Pacu and remove eggs.
Alternatively, simply cooking a tame, fed Pacu's 13 spare eggs over its 25 cycle lifespan into Omelette, at 5600 kcal each due to their large size, provides 2912 kcal per cycle average.
It is possible to sustain a single Pacu-breeder via Algae Distiller-Pufts pathway. One Pacu requires 7.5 kg of Algae per cycle. The 7.5 kg of Algae require 22.5 kg of slime per cycle, which can be covered with some excess by 1 tame Puft. This in turn would need 50 kg of Polluted Oxygen per cycle. Off-gassing such an amount from polluted water would require around 1700 kg of Polluted Water at the surface, or around 2100 kg of bottled Polluted Water for offgassing. It can be supplemented by Polluted Oxygen Vents, Morbs and  Sublimation Stations, although Morbs' production rates are inconsistent.
As the Fish Feeder's Ate From Feeder effect does not depend on the amount of food consumed, it is possible to use very small amounts of food to keep a Pacu happy. This strategy saw more use when its Algae diet was extremely gluttonous.
An alternative option to Algae is to use seeds in your Fish Feeder, as these can be easily gained from a dedicated farm or just from the passive seed gain in your colony's other farms. When making a dedicated farm for the Pacu. The Balm Lily can work well due to the lack of a fertilizer requirement and so only needs dupe labor to harvest. Sleet Wheat and Nosh Sprouts are effective alternatives due to their yields being large numbers of seeds. Spigot Seals can be an excellent source of Bonbon Tree seeds. Finally, Mealwood, Sweatcorn, Pikeapple and Thimble Reeds all grow quickly, and can be effective at producing seeds when paired with a skilled Duplicant. Note that Arbor Acorns/Seakomb Seed cannot be fed to Pacu.
 Each Pacu can be sustained with 2 Seakomb plants. Note that the Polluted Dirt expelled by Pacus is also used as fertilizer for Seakomb but only at 50% efficiency. Alternatively, when Seakomb Leaf is processed into Phyto Oil using Plant Pulverizer, and heated to Algae, one Seakomb plant can sustain 3.5 Pacus, and the Polluted Dirt produced is enough to fully fertilize the Seakomb plant, but this needs a source of Water as it is consumed in the Plant Pulverizer recipe.

A newly-born wild Pacu will live long enough to lay an egg as long as it is not kept with too many other Pacu (up to 10 in 8 tiles of liquid will work). This allows some limited starvation ranching potential, but the yield is rather low considering the investment in materials to set up systems to automatically store the starving Pacu and remove eggs.
Note that wild Pacu can still become Cramped if they are overcrowded when one lays an egg. This can be avoided by moving the egg into another room.

Waterweed is a food plant that produces Lettuce. It grows naturally in Ocean Biome.


== Seed ==
The Waterweed Seed is the seed of Waterweed and it can be obtained by harvesting, uprooting a Waterweed or by digging up a Buried Object within the Ocean Biome.


== Food ==
Each harvest produces 12 kg, 4800 kcals Lettuce which is edible raw, or can be further cooked into Mushroom Wrap, Mushroom Quiche or Frost Burgers.


== Growth ==
Waterweed requires temperature range of 22 °C ↔ 65 °C / 71.6 °F ↔ 149 °F. Waterweed must be submerged in Water, Salt Water or Brine. 


=== Wild ===
A wild Waterweed takes 48 cycles to grow to maturity and produces an averaged 100 kcals per cycle when harvested, meaning you need 10 plants per duplicant.


=== Domestic ===
A domestic Waterweed takes 12 cycles to grow to maturity. Producing 400 kcals per cycle when harvested meaning you need 2.5 plants per duplicant.
Waterweed can be planted in Planter Box, Farm Tile or Hydroponic Farm. It needs to be irrigated with 20 kg/cycle of Salt Water.
Domesticated Waterweed can be sustainably grown by utilizing Salt Water Vent's output. Luckily, the weakest possible vent can support up to 240 plants, although water desalination might cut into that.
In Spaced Out!, Salt Water can also be mined from space POIs.

The Wheezewort is a non-reproducing plant that is found in the Frozen Biome. Wheezeworts are extremely useful for temperature management since they destroy heat from the surrounding environment.


== Seed ==
There are a limited amount of Wheezeworts on the map as they do not produce seeds naturally. However, the Printing Pod can sometimes offer them as Care Packages and seeds can be found as a buried object in the Frozen Biome.
They can also be found in the Printerceptor story trait for 25 Data Banks, increasing by 25 each time you print this seed, up to a maximum of 275.


== Growth ==
A Wheezewort requires temperature range of -60 °C ↔ 95 °C / -76 °F ↔ 203 °F. It has no requirement on air pressure.


=== Wild ===
A wild Wheezewort cools 250 g gas per second.


=== Domestic ===
Wheezeworts can be uprooted and replanted into a Planter Box, Farm Tile, or Hydroponic Farm. It needs to be fertilized with 4 kg/cycle of Phosphorite.
A domestic Wheezewort cools 1 kg gas per second.


== Technical info ==
Wheezeworts cool the gas around them by absorbing the gas (1000 g/s Domestic, 250 g/s wild) in the bottom block of the Wheezewort, and releasing it -5 °C / -9 °F colder. However, the Wheezewort itself weighs 400 kg, and exchanges heat relatively well with the gas, so its own temperature can significantly slow down the overall cooling effect.
The Wheezewort's cooling factor is expressed in absolute temperature rather than energy. Neither heat conductivity, heat capacity, nor volume of the gas being cooled affect the change in temperature. That means that the best way to utilize it is to cool high density of high heat capacity gas - for which Hydrogen is best, resulting in an effective cooling of 12 kDTU/s:
(2.4DTUgK)×(5K)×(1000gs)=12000DTUs
A Wheezewort will never cool any gas below 5°C above its condensation point, meaning it will never directly condense the gas being cooled, but it can cool the gas so much that the plant stifles itself. It can also indirectly cool gas to its condensation point by cooling gas around the other gas below the formers condensation point. This usually only happens in small spaces.


== Atmosphere Comparison ==


== Wheezewort Airpump ==
Due to the Wheezeworts gas interaction, namely, creation of vacuum in its bottom tile, Wheezeworts can be used as unpowered airpumps in one tile wide tunnels. However, such pump will reset itself if the tile that feeds into bottom tile of Wheezeworts gets above 2 kg of pressure or becomes vacuum too.


== Rad Emission ==
In the Spaced Out! DLC, Wheezeworts emit radiation; origin from the lower half of the plant, at 480 rads per cycle in a vacuum. The radiation emission means that they are no longer entirely safe to use for cooling living spaces, however this is usually not a big problem. The radiation also gives Wheezeworts another use: plant mutations.
The radiation given off by Wheezeworts can be captured with Radbolt Generators. In general, the best practice is to have the Wheezewort as close to the generator as possible. However, since Radiation gets absorbed by the Farm Tile (if the Radbolt Generator is underneath the Wheezewort), one should choose a Farm Tile with as little Radiation Absorption as possible.
There is another practical application for the radiation, and that is in disinfecting food storage, since it keeps the food mostly frozen and kills any Food Poisoning germs that may exist on the food.
Using Wheezeworts for plant mutation can be massively useful, especially if there is no other radiation source or it would require power and more resources. Just be mindful not to let the Wheezewort cool the farm too much, or you will have a much bigger problem than the possibility of radiation poisoning.

		
		
		

Note: these values are not applicable to every Wheezewort, and can change up to 2 rads/cycle. It is currently not known what causes this difference, but it likely has to do with their position on the map since a Wheezewort planted in the same place will yield the same result.
